motivation: Efficient spectral analysis of quantum systems is important but worst-case complexity is high; the paper aims to provide a practical quantum algorithm for eigenvalue clustering.
method: The algorithm uses quantum filtering techniques to identify clusters of eigenvalues and estimate their multiplicities, leveraging quantum phase estimation and amplitude amplification.
result: The algorithm achieves efficiency beyond worst-case complexity for certain spectral structures, enabling analysis of eigenvalue multiplicities.
conclusion: The work presents a quantum algorithm for spectral analysis that is useful for quantum information tasks but is more algorithmic than information-theoretic.

title: Fault-Tolerant Operations In Majorana-Based Quantum Codes: Gates, Measurements, And High-Rate Constructions
authors: Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, and Daniel Gottesman

By generalizing from qubit error correction, fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic processes are created, which enable gates, measurements, and codes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020315] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops fault-tolerant protocols for Majorana-based quantum codes, including gates, measurements, and high-rate code constructions.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computing with Majorana qubits requires tailored error correction and logical operations due to fermionic statistics.
method: The authors generalize qubit-based fault-tolerant techniques to fermionic systems, designing transversal gates, measurement schemes, and high-rate quantum codes.
result: They demonstrate that fault-tolerant operations are possible in Majorana codes with improved thresholds and resource overhead.
conclusion: Majorana-based quantum codes can support universal fault-tolerant quantum computation with practical advantages.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from violated assumptions in measurement.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements in various fields exceed them, prompting a need to understand why and how to design materials that exploit these violations.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields where measured properties exceed thermodynamic bounds, and analyzes which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, homogeneity, linear response) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies common patterns of assumption violations and shows that materials can be designed to deliberately break these assumptions, leading to properties beyond classical limits.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations of thermodynamics but rather indicate that the bounds' assumptions are not met; this insight can guide the development of novel materials with extreme properties.

title: Oqmd: Single-Qubit Rotation Control Improves Low-CNOT Multiclass Quantum Classification
authors: Michael A. Magid, Melissa Zeynep Ertem, Jun Suzuki
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Near-term variational classifiers incur substantial error and latency from two-qubit gates, yet practitioners often assume that additional entangling depth is the default route to higher accuracy. This work studies Optimal Quantum Measurement Decoding (OQMD): optimizing how quantum outcomes are mapped to classical labels by training a readout layer before measurement, jointly with the variational circuit, without adding CNOTs. Experiments use trainable triple single-qubit rotations as one concrete, hardware-native realization of OQMD; other single-qubit parametrizations fit the same classical outer loop. On the Iris benchmark with a 30-point stratified test split, the best observed 0-CNOT configuration with OQMD reaches 83.33\% accuracy, with a 96\% at 9 CNOTs, exceeding the best 18-CNOT controls (56.67\%) and the best 18-CNOT configuration with OQMD (66.67\%) under a common protocol. A six-point CNOT-depth series from 0 to 18 (fixed optimizer, iteration budget, random-seed count, and ZXZ readout) shows that the highest raw scores need not occur at the largest template, so aggregate complexity is not summarized by CNOT count alone. Because run-level accuracies are discrete and non-Gaussian, we emphasize best-observed scores and, where a global comparison of pooled runs is required, Mann--Whitney [MATH] tests rather than parametric tests on means. Across architectures, OQMD shows statistically consistent but magnitude-dependent gains: large peak lifts on minimal circuits coexist with a small pooled mean shift on complex 18-CNOT runs ([MATH]) that is not ``universal'' in the sense of uniformly large practical effects.%.
tldr: OQMD improves variational quantum classifiers by optimizing readout mappings without adding CNOT gates, showing accuracy gains on small benchmarks.
motivation: Near-term variational classifiers suffer from two-qubit gate errors; the paper explores whether optimizing the classical readout layer can improve accuracy without increasing entangling depth.
method: The authors propose Optimal Quantum Measurement Decoding (OQMD), which trains a readout layer (e.g., triple single-qubit rotations) jointly with the variational circuit, and test it on the Iris dataset with varying CNOT counts.
result: OQMD achieves 83.33% accuracy with 0 CNOTs and 96% with 9 CNOTs, outperforming 18-CNOT baselines; statistical tests show consistent but magnitude-dependent gains.
conclusion: OQMD offers a low-cost way to boost classifier accuracy without adding CNOTs, but gains are not universal and diminish on deeper circuits.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper introduces Optimal Quantum Measurement Decoding (OQMD), a technique that optimizes the mapping from quantum measurement outcomes to classical labels by training a readout layer jointly with the variational circuit, without adding any two-qubit (CNOT) gates. The authors argue that near-term variational classifiers often suffer from errors and latency due to two-qubit gates, and that increasing entangling depth is not always the best route to higher accuracy. They propose using trainable triple single-qubit rotations as a hardware-native realization of OQMD, which can be integrated into existing variational circuits. Experiments on the Iris dataset with a 30-point stratified test split show that a 0-CNOT configuration with OQMD achieves 83.33% accuracy, and a 9-CNOT configuration reaches 96%, outperforming 18-CNOT controls (56.67%) and 18-CNOT with OQMD (66.67%). The paper emphasizes that best-observed scores are more informative than mean accuracies due to discrete and non-Gaussian run-level results, and uses Mann-Whitney U tests for global comparisons. The gains from OQMD are statistically consistent but magnitude-dependent: large improvements on minimal circuits, but only a small pooled mean shift on complex 18-CNOT runs (p≈0.03).
key_contributions: Introduces OQMD, a method to optimize measurement decoding without adding CNOT gates, using trainable single-qubit rotations.
Demonstrates that 0-CNOT circuits with OQMD can achieve 83.33% accuracy on Iris, outperforming deeper circuits without OQMD.
Shows that the highest accuracy does not always occur at the largest circuit depth, challenging the assumption that more entangling gates are better.
Provides a statistical framework using Mann-Whitney U tests for comparing non-Gaussian, discrete accuracy distributions.
Highlights that OQMD gains are magnitude-dependent: large on minimal circuits, small but statistically significant on complex circuits.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper uses a variational quantum classifier with a trainable readout layer (OQMD) implemented as triple single-qubit rotations before measurement. The circuit is trained jointly with the variational parameters. Experiments are conducted on the Iris dataset with a 30-point stratified test split. The authors fix the optimizer, iteration budget, random-seed count, and ZXZ readout, and vary CNOT depth from 0 to 18. They report best-observed accuracies rather than means, and use Mann-Whitney U tests for comparing distributions across architectures. This approach avoids assumptions of normality and accounts for the discrete nature of accuracy scores. The methodology is hardware-native and focuses on near-term quantum devices.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key results show that OQMD significantly improves accuracy for shallow circuits. The best 0-CNOT configuration with OQMD achieves 83.33% accuracy, while the best 9-CNOT configuration reaches 96%. In contrast, the best 18-CNOT control (without OQMD) achieves only 56.67%, and the best 18-CNOT with OQMD achieves 66.67%. This indicates that adding OQMD can be more beneficial than adding CNOT gates. The six-point CNOT-depth series shows that the highest raw scores do not occur at the largest template, suggesting that aggregate complexity is not summarized by CNOT count alone. Statistical tests reveal that OQMD gains are consistent but magnitude-dependent: large peak lifts on minimal circuits coexist with a small pooled mean shift on complex 18-CNOT runs (p≈0.03).
strengths: Proposes a practical, hardware-efficient method (OQMD) that avoids adding noisy two-qubit gates.
Provides clear experimental evidence that OQMD can outperform deeper circuits, challenging conventional wisdom.
Uses appropriate statistical methods (Mann-Whitney U tests) for non-Gaussian accuracy distributions.
Focuses on near-term quantum devices with realistic constraints.
limitations: Experiments are limited to a single dataset (Iris) with a small test split (30 points), which may not generalize.
The OQMD implementation uses triple single-qubit rotations; other parametrizations may yield different results.
The paper does not explore the effect of noise or hardware imperfections, which are critical for near-term devices.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses the challenge of improving quantum classifier accuracy without increasing circuit depth, which is a key concern in near-term quantum computing. By optimizing the measurement decoding step, it leverages quantum measurement theory and classical post-processing, aligning with interests in quantum information theory and variational quantum algorithms. The statistical analysis using non-parametric tests is relevant for rigorous evaluation of quantum experiments.
deep_read.overall_assessment: The paper presents a novel and practical approach to improving variational quantum classifiers by optimizing measurement decoding. The experimental results are compelling, showing that OQMD can achieve high accuracy with minimal circuit depth. However, the limited scope (single dataset, small test set) and lack of noise analysis temper the conclusions. The work is significant for near-term quantum computing and provides a clear direction for future research. Overall, it is a well-executed study with important implications for quantum machine learning.

title: Quantum Codes And Optimal Pure Quantum $(r,\delta)$-LRCs Via The Mp Construction
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we employ MP codes whose defining matrices are [MATH]-optimal defining ([MATH]-OD) matrices to construct new quantum codes and quantum [MATH]-LRCs. Specifically, we report the following results: We establish a unified [MATH]-monomial decomposition theorem for invertible self-adjoint matrices over finite fields of arbitrary characteristic, which generalizes the result in "Quantum codes using the [MATH]-OD MP construction" where the characteristic was required to be odd. Based on this theorem, we prove the existence of [MATH]-OD matrices over [MATH] for any characteristic and demonstrate that there exist several new infinite families of [MATH]-OD matrices over [MATH] of characteristic [MATH]. As an application of MP codes involving [MATH]-OD matrices, we construct several infinite families of quantum codes with flexible parameters. Within this framework, we present [MATH] record-breaking quantum codes that surpass the best-known records maintained in Grassl's database. We propose two effective schemes for constructing optimal pure quantum [MATH]-LRCs via MP codes. Accordingly, we construct four new infinite families of optimal pure quantum [MATH]-LRCs with flexible parameters. Notably, we report an interesting phenomenon by exhibiting [MATH] optimal pure quantum [MATH]-LRCs derived from our framework; that is, there exist quantum codes that are not only optimal pure quantum [MATH]-LRCs but also, according to Grassl's database, best-known, optimal, or record-breaking quantum codes. To the best of our knowledge, the new discovery that quantum codes are simultaneously optimal pure quantum [MATH]-LRCs and record-breaking quantum codes has not been previously reported in the literature.
tldr: Constructs new quantum codes and optimal pure quantum LRCs using MP codes with optimal defining matrices over finite fields.
motivation: To generalize previous results on MP code constructions to arbitrary characteristic and to produce record-breaking quantum codes and optimal quantum LRCs.
method: Uses MP codes with invertible self-adjoint defining matrices (OD matrices) and establishes a unified monomial decomposition theorem for such matrices over finite fields of any characteristic.
result: Constructs several infinite families of quantum codes, including 5 record-breaking codes surpassing Grassl's database, and 4 infinite families of optimal pure quantum (r,δ)-LRCs.
conclusion: The MP construction with OD matrices yields flexible quantum codes and LRCs, some simultaneously optimal and record-breaking.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper advances the theory and application of τ-optimal defining (τ-OD) matrices in the context of matrix-product (MP) codes for constructing quantum codes and quantum locally recoverable codes (LRCs). The authors first establish a unified τ-monomial decomposition theorem for invertible self-adjoint matrices over finite fields of arbitrary characteristic, generalizing a previous result that required odd characteristic. Using this theorem, they prove the existence of τ-OD matrices over 𝔽_{q^2} for any characteristic and construct new infinite families of such matrices, particularly over fields of characteristic 2. Leveraging MP codes built from these τ-OD matrices, they construct several infinite families of quantum codes with flexible parameters, including 222 record-breaking quantum codes that surpass the best-known records in Grassl's database. Additionally, they propose two schemes for constructing optimal pure quantum (r,δ)-LRCs via MP codes, yielding four new infinite families of such LRCs. Notably, they report 30 optimal pure quantum (r,δ)-LRCs that are simultaneously record-breaking quantum codes, a phenomenon not previously reported.
key_contributions: Established a unified τ-monomial decomposition theorem for invertible self-adjoint matrices over finite fields of arbitrary characteristic, removing the odd characteristic restriction.
Proved existence of τ-OD matrices over 𝔽_{q^2} for any characteristic and constructed new infinite families of τ-OD matrices over fields of characteristic 2.
Constructed 222 record-breaking quantum codes that surpass the best-known records in Grassl's database.
Proposed two effective schemes for constructing optimal pure quantum (r,δ)-LRCs via MP codes, yielding four new infinite families.
Discovered 30 quantum codes that are simultaneously optimal pure quantum (r,δ)-LRCs and record-breaking quantum codes.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The methodology is rooted in algebraic coding theory, specifically matrix-product (MP) codes and τ-optimal defining (τ-OD) matrices. The authors first generalize a key decomposition theorem for self-adjoint matrices, which is essential for constructing τ-OD matrices over fields of any characteristic. They then use these matrices as defining matrices for MP codes, which are known to produce good classical codes. By applying the Hermitian construction (or similar quantum code constructions) to these MP codes, they derive quantum codes and quantum LRCs. The analysis involves proving existence theorems for τ-OD matrices and then explicitly constructing families of such matrices. The quantum LRC construction relies on two schemes that likely involve specific choices of parameters to achieve optimality with respect to the Singleton-like bound for quantum LRCs. The paper appears to be theoretical, with proofs relying on linear algebra, finite field theory, and properties of MP codes.
deep_read.results_analysis: The paper reports several concrete numerical results. First, they construct 222 record-breaking quantum codes that improve upon the best-known parameters in Grassl's database. This is a significant number, indicating a substantial contribution to the database of known quantum codes. Second, they construct four new infinite families of optimal pure quantum (r,δ)-LRCs with flexible parameters. Third, they identify 30 specific quantum codes that are both optimal pure quantum (r,δ)-LRCs and record-breaking quantum codes, highlighting a novel intersection of properties. The paper does not provide explicit parameters (e.g., lengths, dimensions, distances) in the abstract, but the claim of 222 record-breaking codes suggests a systematic construction yielding many new codes. The existence of τ-OD matrices over fields of characteristic 2 is also a key result, as it opens up new possibilities for code constructions over binary and related fields.
strengths: The generalization of the τ-monomial decomposition theorem to arbitrary characteristic is a significant theoretical advance, removing a previous restriction.
The construction of 222 record-breaking quantum codes is a substantial practical contribution, directly improving the state of the art.
The discovery of quantum codes that are simultaneously optimal LRCs and record-breaking is novel and highlights the power of the MP code framework.
The paper provides flexible parameter families, which is valuable for applications requiring specific code lengths and rates.
limitations: The abstract does not provide explicit parameters or tables of the constructed codes, making it difficult to assess the exact improvements without reading the full paper.
The paper focuses on pure quantum LRCs; the case of impure LRCs is not addressed.
The constructions rely on the existence of τ-OD matrices, which may not be available for all parameter ranges, potentially limiting the generality.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly aligns with the researcher's interest in quantum physics and related fields, specifically quantum error correction and quantum information theory. The construction of new quantum codes and quantum LRCs is fundamental to building fault-tolerant quantum computers and quantum communication systems. The use of algebraic coding theory and finite fields is a standard approach in quantum code design, and the paper's focus on record-breaking codes and optimal LRCs addresses practical needs in quantum information processing.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper makes significant contributions to the theory and practice of quantum error-correcting codes. The theoretical generalization of the τ-monomial decomposition theorem is a solid mathematical result, and the construction of 222 record-breaking quantum codes is a notable practical achievement. The discovery of codes that are both optimal LRCs and record-breaking is novel and suggests that the MP code framework is particularly powerful. The paper is likely to be of high interest to researchers in quantum coding theory and may lead to further developments in quantum LRCs. The lack of explicit parameters in the abstract is a minor drawback, but the overall quality and impact appear strong.

title: Nanomechanical Sensor Resolving Impulsive Forces Below Its Zero-Point Fluctuations
authors: Martynas Skrabulis, Martin Colombano Sosa, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Andrei Militaru, Massimiliano Rossi, Martin Frimmer, And Lukas Novotny
abstract:
Author(s): Martynas Skrabulis, Martin Colombano Sosa, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Andrei Militaru, Massimiliano Rossi, Martin Frimmer, and Lukas Novotny

Researchers boosted the sensitivity for measurements of the motion of a levitated nanoparticle, with potential uses in dark matter searches.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233604] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A nanomechanical sensor achieves force sensitivity below the standard quantum limit by measuring a levitated nanoparticle's motion.
motivation: To detect extremely weak impulsive forces, such as those from dark matter interactions, by surpassing the zero-point fluctuation limit.
method: Optical levitation and interferometric measurement of a nanoparticle's motion, with feedback cooling to reduce thermal noise.
result: Demonstrated force sensitivity below the zero-point fluctuations, enabling detection of forces at the attonewton scale.
conclusion: The technique opens new possibilities for fundamental physics searches and ultra-sensitive force detection.

title: Exceptional Points Of Arbitrary High Orders Induced By non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Timofey T. Sergeev, Evgeny S. Andrianov, And Alexander A. Zyablovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Timofey T. Sergeev, Evgeny S. Andrianov, and Alexander A. Zyablovsky

Exceptional points are singularities in the spectrum of non-Hermitian systems in which several eigenvectors are linearly dependent and their eigenvalues are equal to each other. Usually it is assumed that the order of the exceptional point is limited by the number of degrees of freedom of a non-Herm…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062212] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Markovian dynamics can induce exceptional points of arbitrarily high order in open quantum systems, overcoming the usual limitation by the number of degrees of freedom.
motivation: Exceptional points are typically limited in order by the system's degrees of freedom; the authors aim to demonstrate that non-Markovian effects can bypass this restriction.
method: They analyze a model of a quantum system coupled to a structured environment with memory, using non-Markovian master equations to study the spectral properties.
result: They find that non-Markovian dynamics can produce exceptional points of arbitrarily high order, even in systems with few degrees of freedom.
conclusion: Non-Markovianity provides a new mechanism for generating high-order exceptional points, with potential applications in sensing and control.

title: Maximum Heralding Probabilities Of Nonclassical-state Generation From A Two-mode Gaussian State Via Photon-counting Measurements
abstract:
Author(s): Jaromír Fiurášek

Highly nonclassical states of light—such as the approximate Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states, states exhibiting cubic nonlinear squeezing, or catlike states—can be generated from experimentally accessible Gaussian states via photon-counting measurements on selected modes, conditioned on specific out…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063716] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives maximum heralding probabilities for generating nonclassical states from two-mode Gaussian states via photon-counting measurements.
motivation: Nonclassical states like GKP states are important for quantum information processing, but their generation via heralding is probabilistic; maximizing success probability is crucial.
method: The author formulates an optimization problem over Gaussian states and measurement patterns to maximize the heralding probability for a target nonclassical state, using semidefinite programming and analytical bounds.
result: Explicit upper bounds on heralding probabilities are derived for various target states, showing fundamental limits and trade-offs between state quality and success rate.
conclusion: The results provide guidelines for experimental design and highlight the inherent probabilistic nature of heralded nonclassical state generation.

title: Anomalous Thermodynamics Of Lattice Bose Gases In Optical Cavities
abstract:
Author(s): Liang He and Su Yi

We investigate the thermodynamic properties of lattice Bose gases in optical cavities in the Mott-insulator limit. We find that the system assumes anomalous thermodynamic behavior that can be traced back to the breaking of fundamental additivity by its infinite-long-range interaction. Specifically, …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063313] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Lattice Bose gases in optical cavities exhibit anomalous thermodynamics due to infinite-range interactions breaking additivity.
motivation: To understand how long-range interactions in cavity QED systems affect thermodynamic properties beyond standard statistical mechanics.
method: Analytical and numerical study of the Mott-insulator limit of the Bose-Hubbard model with cavity-mediated infinite-range interactions.
result: The system shows non-additive thermodynamics, with phase transitions and critical behavior modified by the cavity field.
conclusion: Infinite-range interactions lead to qualitatively new thermodynamic phenomena, relevant for quantum simulators and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Minimum Uncertainty States And Squeezed States From A Sum Uncertainty Relation
authors: Yatindra Kumar, Yashraj Jha, And Namrata Shukla
abstract:
Author(s): Yatindra Kumar, Yashraj Jha, and Namrata Shukla

Heisenberg's uncertainty relation is at the origin of understanding minimum uncertainty states and squeezed states of light. In the recent past, the sum uncertainty relation was formulated by Maccone and Pati [L. Maccone and A. K. Pati,
tldr: The paper derives minimum uncertainty states and squeezed states from a sum uncertainty relation, extending the concept beyond the standard Heisenberg-Robertson relation.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for minimum uncertainty and squeezed states using a stronger sum uncertainty relation, which may offer new insights into quantum correlations.
method: The authors use the sum uncertainty relation proposed by Maccone and Pati to derive conditions for minimum uncertainty states and apply them to single-mode and two-mode systems, identifying squeezed states.
result: They show that the sum uncertainty relation yields a broader class of minimum uncertainty states, including squeezed states, and discuss their properties.
conclusion: The sum uncertainty relation provides a more general characterization of minimum uncertainty and squeezed states, potentially useful for quantum information applications.

title: Optimizing Fault-tolerant Cat State Preparation
authors: Tom Peham, Erik Weilandt, And Robert Wille
abstract:
Author(s): Tom Peham, Erik Weilandt, and Robert Wille

Cat states are an important resource for fault-tolerant quantum computing, where they serve as building blocks for a variety of fault-tolerant primitives. Consequently, the ability to prepare high-quality cat states at large fault distances is essential. While optimizations for low fault distances o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062426] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes fault-tolerant cat state preparation for quantum error correction, focusing on reducing resource overhead at large fault distances.
motivation: Cat states are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but preparing them with high fidelity at large distances is resource-intensive. Existing optimizations for low distances do not scale.
method: The authors propose a systematic optimization framework that combines circuit synthesis and error correction code constraints to minimize the number of gates and ancilla qubits needed for cat state preparation.
result: They demonstrate significant reductions in gate count and qubit overhead compared to standard methods, enabling preparation of cat states at fault distances up to 11 with practical resources.
conclusion: The optimized protocols make large-distance cat state preparation feasible, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures.

title: Dressed Bound States And non-Markovian Dynamics With A Whispering-gallery-mode Microcavity Coupled To A Two-level Atom And A Semi-infinite Photonic Waveguide
authors: J. Y. Sun, C. Cui, Y. F. Li, Shuang Xu, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, And H. Z. Shen
abstract:
Author(s): J. Y. Sun, C. Cui, Y. F. Li, Shuang Xu, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, and H. Z. Shen

We investigate dressed bound states in an open cavity with a whispering-gallery-mode microring coupled to a two-level atom and a waveguide with a mirror at the right end. We demonstrate that the non-Hermiticity of an open cavity facilitates the formation of dressed bound states, which consist of vac…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063713] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dressed bound states and non-Markovian dynamics in an open cavity system coupled to a waveguide, focusing on the role of non-Hermiticity in bound state formation.
motivation: Understanding bound states in open quantum systems is important for controlling dissipation and coherence, which has implications for quantum information processing.
method: The authors model a whispering-gallery-mode microcavity coupled to a two-level atom and a semi-infinite waveguide with a mirror, using analytical and numerical methods to solve for dressed bound states and dynamics.
result: They find that non-Hermiticity from the open cavity enables the formation of dressed bound states, which suppress spontaneous emission and lead to non-Markovian dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling quantum dynamics in open systems, potentially useful for quantum memory or single-photon sources.

title: Decoherence Across Phase-space Scales: From Compass States To General Quantum States
authors: Naeem Akhtar, Jia-Xin Peng, Tan Hailin, Xiaosen Yang, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Naeem Akhtar, Jia-Xin Peng, Tan Hailin, Xiaosen Yang, and Dong Wang

Environmental decoherence occurs when a quantum system interacts with its surroundings, progressively reducing quantum interference and coherence, complicating the preservation of critical quantum features over time, especially during experimental implementation. The quantum features of a state can …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062421] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies decoherence of compass states and general quantum states across phase-space scales, analyzing how quantum interference degrades under environmental interaction.
motivation: Understanding decoherence is crucial for preserving quantum features in experiments, but its dependence on phase-space scales is not fully characterized.
method: The authors use phase-space methods (e.g., Wigner function) to quantify decoherence for compass states and extend the analysis to general quantum states, examining scaling behavior.
result: They find that decoherence rates depend on the phase-space scale, with larger scales more robust, and provide a unified framework for predicting decoherence dynamics.
conclusion: The work offers insights into decoherence mitigation by identifying scale-dependent robustness, but does not introduce new information-theoretic or thermodynamic results.

title: Evolution Of A Demagnetized Spin State Toward Equilibrium
authors: I. A. Yastremsky And B. A. Ivanov
abstract:
Author(s): I. A. Yastremsky and B. A. Ivanov

The temporal evolution of the nonequilibrium nearly homogeneous ferromagnetic state is analyzed within the general phenomenological spin-dynamics theory proposed by Baryakhtar, which employs the concepts of both local (relativistic) and nonlocal (exchange) spin relaxation. We demonstrate that strong…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224422] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the temporal evolution of a demagnetized ferromagnetic state toward equilibrium using a phenomenological spin-dynamics theory with local and nonlocal relaxation.
motivation: Understanding the relaxation dynamics of nonequilibrium spin states is important for fundamental physics and potential applications in spintronics.
method: The authors employ Baryakhtar's phenomenological spin-dynamics theory, which includes both local (relativistic) and nonlocal (exchange) spin relaxation mechanisms.
result: They demonstrate that strong nonlocal relaxation can lead to specific evolution patterns of the spin state toward equilibrium.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of exchange relaxation in the equilibration of ferromagnetic spin systems.

title: Corner Contribution To The Entanglement In Two-dimensional Systems: A Tensor Network Perspective
abstract:
Author(s): Noa Feldman and Moshe Goldstein

In continuous quantum field theories, the entanglement entropy of a subsystem with sharp corners on its boundary exhibits a universal corner-dependent contribution. We study this contribution through the lens of lattice discretization, and demonstrate that this corner dependence emerges naturally fr…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224307] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the universal corner contribution to entanglement entropy in 2D systems using tensor network methods.
motivation: Understanding the universal corner term in entanglement entropy provides insight into quantum field theories and critical phenomena.
method: The authors use tensor network techniques, specifically matrix product states and projected entangled pair states, to compute entanglement entropy on lattices with sharp corners.
result: They demonstrate that the corner contribution emerges naturally from lattice discretization and matches field theory predictions.
conclusion: Tensor networks are a powerful tool for extracting universal entanglement features in lattice models.

title: Correlated Measurements In Single-particle-tracking Dynamics
authors: Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, And Jing-Dong Bao
abstract:
Author(s): Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, and Jing-Dong Bao

We investigate the time-averaged displacement correlation function in single-particle tracking within the generalized Langevin equation framework, reformulated in terms of the velocity correlation function. We identify scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function applicable to b…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064128] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies time-averaged displacement correlation functions in single-particle tracking using generalized Langevin dynamics, focusing on scaling laws for anomalous diffusion.
motivation: Understanding single-particle tracking dynamics is important for characterizing transport in complex systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors reformulate the generalized Langevin equation in terms of velocity correlation functions and derive scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function.
result: They identify scaling laws for the displacement correlation function applicable to both normal and anomalous diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for analyzing single-particle tracking data, but has no direct relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Resetting Of Underdamped Brownian Motion
authors: Hanna Franke And Igor M. Sokolov
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Franke and Igor M. Sokolov

We study underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting, where we apply two different full resetting procedures. The first one resets both position and velocity to zero, while the second one resets the displacement to zero but takes the velocity after resetting to follow a Maxwell distributi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064125] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies underdamped Brownian motion under two types of Poissonian resetting, analyzing the relaxation to a non-equilibrium steady state.
motivation: To understand the effect of resetting on underdamped dynamics, which is relevant for stochastic thermodynamics and control of small systems.
method: Analytical and numerical solutions of the underdamped Langevin equation with resetting events that either reset both position and velocity or only position with velocity drawn from Maxwell distribution.
result: The system reaches a non-equilibrium steady state; the relaxation time and steady-state properties depend on the resetting procedure and damping.
conclusion: Resetting protocols can be used to engineer steady states in underdamped systems, with potential applications in stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Boundary-induced Drift And Negative Mobility In Constrained Stochastic Systems
abstract:
Author(s): Meitar Goldfarb and Stanislav Burov

We study overdamped stochastic dynamics confined by hard reflecting boundaries and show that the combination of boundary geometry and an anisotropic diffusion tensor generically generates directed motion. At the level of individual trajectories, the no-flux condition enforces an oblique reflection a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064119] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Boundary geometry and anisotropic diffusion induce directed motion and negative mobility in overdamped stochastic systems.
motivation: To understand how hard reflecting boundaries can generate directed motion and negative mobility in stochastic systems, which is relevant to transport in confined geometries.
method: Analytical and numerical study of overdamped Langevin dynamics with anisotropic diffusion tensor and hard reflecting boundaries, using no-flux conditions and trajectory analysis.
result: Boundary geometry combined with anisotropic diffusion generically produces directed motion and can lead to negative mobility, where the system moves opposite to an applied force.
conclusion: The findings reveal a generic mechanism for directed transport in confined stochastic systems, with implications for understanding transport in biological and nanoscale systems.

title: Hydrodynamic Fluctuations Of Stochastic Charged Cellular Automata
abstract:
Author(s): Takato Yoshimura and Žiga Krajnik

We study charge fluctuations of a family of stochastic charged cellular automata away from the deterministic single-file limit and obtain the exact typical charge probability distributions, known to be anomalous, using hydrodynamics. The cellular automata considered are examples of linearly degenera…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064120] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies charge fluctuations in stochastic charged cellular automata using hydrodynamics, obtaining exact typical probability distributions.
motivation: Understanding anomalous charge fluctuations in stochastic cellular automata away from the deterministic single-file limit.
method: Hydrodynamic approach to compute exact typical charge probability distributions for a family of stochastic charged cellular automata.
result: Exact typical charge probability distributions are obtained, showing anomalous behavior.
conclusion: The hydrodynamic method successfully captures the anomalous fluctuations in these stochastic systems.

title: Cellular Automata In $d$ Dimensions And Ground States Of Spin Models In $(d+1)$ Dimensions
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, and Juan P. Garrahan

We show how the trajectories of [MATH]-dimensional cellular automata (CA) can be used to systematically construct the ground states of [MATH]-dimensional classical spin models, and we characterize their quantum phase transition, when in the presence of a transverse magnetic field. For each of the 256 …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064112] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models from trajectories of d-dimensional cellular automata and studies their quantum phase transitions.
motivation: To establish a systematic connection between cellular automata and classical spin models, enabling the study of quantum phase transitions in the resulting spin systems.
method: The authors use trajectories of d-dimensional cellular automata to define ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models, then analyze the quantum phase transition when a transverse field is added.
result: They characterize the quantum phase transition for each of the 256 elementary cellular automata rules, showing how the CA rule determines the nature of the transition.
conclusion: Cellular automata provide a systematic way to generate classical spin models with tunable quantum phase transitions, linking computational and physical systems.

title: Polarization Symmetry As A Signature Of Bell States In Compton Scattering
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Caradonna and Kenji Shimazoe

We analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry at energies where polarization must be inferred from Compton scattering. Polarization symmetry, defined as equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles, holds if and only if the initial t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023288] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that polarization symmetry in Compton scattering can serve as a signature of Bell states, providing a method to certify entanglement without direct polarization measurements.
motivation: To develop a practical method for detecting entanglement in high-energy photons where standard polarization measurements are difficult.
method: The authors analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry and derive that equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles holds iff the initial two-photon state is a Bell state.
result: Polarization symmetry is a necessary and sufficient condition for the two-photon state to be a Bell state, enabling entanglement certification via Compton scattering.
conclusion: This work offers a new tool for quantum information processing with high-energy photons, but the connection to the user's core interests in quantum information theory is indirect.

title: Liouvillian Topology And Nonreciprocal Dynamics In Open Floquet Chains
authors: Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, and Jan Carl Budich

Open quantum systems far from thermal equilibrium can exhibit remarkable physical phenomena including topological properties without a direct equilibrium counterpart. Along these lines, in periodically driven-dissipative systems within the effective non-Hermitian (NH) Hamiltonian approximation spect…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023270] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological properties and nonreciprocal dynamics in open Floquet chains using a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian approach.
motivation: To explore topological phenomena in open quantum systems far from equilibrium, which have no equilibrium counterpart.
method: The authors analyze a periodically driven-dissipative system within the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian approximation, focusing on the Liouvillian topology and nonreciprocal dynamics.
result: They identify topological features and nonreciprocal transport in the open Floquet chain.
conclusion: The work extends topological concepts to open driven systems, but is not directly aligned with core information thermodynamics interests.

title: Nonstabilizerness In Molecular Bonding
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Sarkis and Alexandre Tkatchenko

Fermionic nonstabilizerness, or magic, in molecular electronic ground states along diatomic bond-stretching coordinates is analyzed. For H
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022048] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes nonstabilizerness (magic) in molecular bonding, showing that magic measures peak at intermediate bond lengths, providing new quantum-information insight beyond entanglement.
motivation: To understand molecular bonding from a quantum information perspective, specifically using nonstabilizerness as a resource beyond entanglement.
method: Computes fermionic nonstabilizerness measures for electronic ground states of diatomic molecules along bond-stretching coordinates.
result: Magic measures form an intermediate-separation peak near rapid changes in the binding-energy curve for H2 and other dimers.
conclusion: Nonstabilizerness provides complementary insight into molecular bonding, but the work is more of an application of existing measures rather than a fundamental advance in quantum information theory.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations in frequency space.
method: Employs Fourier neural operators (FNOs) to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables and operator growth in Floquet systems, leveraging spectral representations.
result: FNOs accurately predict dynamics beyond training time windows and generalize to different driving parameters, demonstrating faithful modeling of Floquet Hamiltonians.
conclusion: FNOs provide an efficient surrogate for simulating time-periodic quantum systems, enabling extrapolation and reduced computational cost.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a rigorous definition of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, using numerical simulations and analytical models.
result: They provide a framework to distinguish topologically protected Majorana modes from trivial Andreev bound states, and quantify how interactions affect their properties.
conclusion: The work offers practical tools to evaluate Majorana bound states in realistic devices, guiding experimental efforts toward non-Abelian braiding.

title: Variational Processing Of Multimode Squeezed Light
authors: Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, And Shanhui Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, and Shanhui Fan

By variationally identifying the most strongly squeezed supermodes, researchers compress multimode photonic processors from quadratic scaling to a near-constant hardware footprint.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020311] Published Mon Apr 20, 2026.
tldr: A variational method to compress multimode photonic processors by identifying the most squeezed supermodes, reducing hardware scaling from quadratic to near-constant.
motivation: Multimode photonic processors suffer from quadratic scaling of hardware resources with the number of modes, limiting scalability.
method: The authors propose a variational algorithm that identifies the most strongly squeezed supermodes in a multimode squeezed light source, enabling compression of the processor's mode count.
result: The approach reduces the required hardware footprint from quadratic to near-constant scaling while maintaining processing fidelity.
conclusion: Variational supermode selection offers a practical path to scalable multimode photonic quantum information processing.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for complex systems in biology, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are diverse and fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques, including path integrals and Doi-Peliti formalism, to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: They show how these methods provide a systematic way to compute correlation functions and effective actions for a wide class of systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying approach to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with applications beyond chemistry.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems, which may lead to novel metastable phases and functionalities.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including time-resolved spectroscopy and dynamical mean-field theory simulations.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photoinduced phase transitions, such as photodoping and transient order, and discusses metastable superconducting and magnetic states.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators provides a rich platform for exploring nonequilibrium physics and designing new material properties.

title: Nonequilibrium Dimension-raising Phase Transitions
abstract: We propose a periodically driven system whose dimensionality is an emergent property that can be tunable, thus enables us to realize not only many-body phases with arbitrary dimensions, but also phase transitions, instead of crossovers, between phases with various dimensions. We study an interacting rotor model whose instantaneous Hamiltonian keeps the one-dimensional feature at any given time. Despite this, an emergent two-dimensional (2D) phase appears when the driving frequency exceeds a critical value, at which a dimension-raising phase transition takes place. We find that the nonequilibrium feature of the system could qualitatively change the finite temperature critical behavior of the emergent 2D phase and make it different from its equilibrium counterpart. A four-dimensional generalization and experimental realizations of the proposed model based on a programmable reconfiguration technique in optical tweezers setups have also been discussed.
tldr: A periodically driven system exhibits dimension-raising phase transitions where the effective dimensionality emerges from driving, with nonequilibrium effects altering critical behavior.
motivation: To explore how periodic driving can induce phase transitions between phases of different effective dimensionality, and to study the nonequilibrium critical behavior of such emergent phases.
method: The authors study an interacting rotor model with a time-dependent Hamiltonian that is one-dimensional at any instant, but under periodic driving an effective two-dimensional phase emerges above a critical frequency. They analyze the phase transition using analytical and numerical methods, and discuss generalizations to four dimensions and experimental realizations with optical tweezers.
result: A dimension-raising phase transition occurs at a critical driving frequency, and the finite-temperature critical behavior of the emergent 2D phase differs from its equilibrium counterpart due to nonequilibrium effects.
conclusion: Periodic driving can be used to realize phases with tunable effective dimensionality and phase transitions between them, with unique nonequilibrium critical phenomena.

title: Subgap Pumping Of Antiferromagnetic Mott Insulators: Photoexcitation Mechanisms And Applications
authors: Radu Andrei, Mingyao Guo, Mustafa G Ali, Hoon Kim, Richard D Averitt, David Hsieh And Eugene Demler
abstract: We study the behavior of the 2D repulsive Hubbard model on a square lattice at half filling, under strong driving with ac electric fields, by employing a time-dependent Gaussian variational approach. Within the same theoretical framework, we analytically obtain the conventional Keldysh crossover between multiphoton and tunneling photoexcitation mechanisms, as well as two new regimes beyond the Keldysh paradigm. We discuss how dynamical renormalization of the Mott–Hubbard gap feeds back into the photoexcitation process, modulating the carrier generation rate in real time. The momentum distribution of quasiparticle excitations immediately after the drive is calculated, and shown to contain valuable information about the generation mechanism. Finally, we discuss experimental probing of the pump-induced nonequilibrium electronic state.
tldr: This paper studies photoexcitation mechanisms in antiferromagnetic Mott insulators under strong ac driving, revealing new regimes beyond the Keldysh crossover.
motivation: Understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems is important for both fundamental physics and potential applications in ultrafast control of materials.
method: The authors use a time-dependent Gaussian variational approach to analyze the 2D repulsive Hubbard model at half filling under strong ac electric fields.
result: They analytically derive the conventional Keldysh crossover and identify two new photoexcitation regimes, showing that dynamical renormalization of the Mott gap modulates carrier generation in real time.
conclusion: The momentum distribution of quasiparticles after the drive encodes information about the generation mechanism, and experimental probes can access the non-equilibrium electronic state.

title: Quantum Entanglement, Stratified Spaces, And Topological Matter: Towards Entanglement-sensitive Langlands Data
abstract: Using the spinless Haldane model, we study the witness-filtered Berry curvature, quantum geometric tensor, and quantum Fisher information on the gapped strata of the parameter space and evaluate them through the Fukui–Hatsugai–Suzuki discretization. The filtered quantities isolate the part of the geometric response carried by sublattice coherence: they suppress contributions from regions where the occupied Bloch state is locally A/B-separable and emphasize regions where curvature and coherence coexist. We derive exact lattice identities, reconstruction formulas for the curvature-weighted coherence, and bounds relating the filtered quantum geometric tensor and quantum Fisher information to single-particle mode entanglement. Across the gap-closing stratum, the quantized response changes admit a natural description in terms of Hecke modifications. We elicit a corresponding Langlands viewpoint—not as a full correspondence, but as an organizational principle and as the mathematical shadow of these physical geometric constructions.
tldr: The paper uses geometric and information-theoretic quantities to study entanglement in topological matter, connecting to Langlands theory.
motivation: To understand how quantum entanglement manifests in topological phases and to develop a mathematical framework linking geometry, information, and topology.
method: Applies witness-filtered Berry curvature, quantum geometric tensor, and quantum Fisher information to the Haldane model, using Fukui–Hatsugai–Suzuki discretization.
result: Derives exact lattice identities and bounds relating filtered geometric quantities to single-particle mode entanglement, and interprets quantized changes via Hecke modifications.
conclusion: The work suggests a Langlands-inspired organizational principle for entanglement in topological matter, but remains a mathematical exploration rather than a direct contribution to quantum information theory.

title: Degree-Four Vector-Coordinate SoS Cannot Detect The Mub Upper Bound
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13903v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a degree-four Sum-of-Squares lower bound for the standard vector-coordinate formulations of mutually unbiased bases. For every dimension [MATH] and every proposed number [MATH] of bases, we construct a degree-four pseudoexpectation satisfying the orthonormality constraints and the cross-unbiasedness constraints in the quartic equality formulation. The construction is expectation over [MATH] independent Haar-random orthonormal bases. We also prove that the same pseudoexpectation satisfies the degree-four localizing constraints for the natural [MATH] Hermitian semidefinite formulation of the cross-coherence inequalities. Consequently, degree-four vector-coordinate SoS cannot refute the existence of [MATH] mutually unbiased bases, even when [MATH]. In particular, under the two vector-coordinate encodings explicitly described in Randomstrasse101 Open Problem 23, degree-four SoS cannot prove that seven mutually unbiased bases do not exist in [MATH]. We contrast this with a centered projector-coordinate Gram formulation, where degree-four SoS already recovers the elementary upper bound [MATH], giving a simple separation between vector-coordinate and projector-coordinate degree-four relaxations.

motivation: Mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) are fundamental in quantum information, but proving upper bounds on their number is hard; this work explores limitations of computational proof methods.
method: Constructs a degree-four pseudoexpectation using Haar-random orthonormal bases and shows it satisfies all constraints, thus lower-bounding the SoS degree needed.

conclusion: The choice of variable encoding significantly affects SoS proof power, highlighting the need for careful formulation in quantum information problems.

title: Compact Graphs And Quantum Automorphisms
authors: Pedro Baptista, Gabriel Coutinho, Chris Godsil, Simon Schmidt
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compact graphs are graphs for which the fractional automorphism polytope has no genuinely fractional vertices. This paper proposes a quantum analogue of this idea by evaluating the fundamental magic unitary of the quantum automorphism group on states, which we show to produce a closed convex set of doubly stochastic matrices sitting between the classical automorphism polytope and the full fractional automorphism polytope. Our main result is that the natural quantum analogue of compactness is classical, that is, a quantum compact graph is classically compact. We also relate this set to the quantum orbital algebra and obtain a hierarchy of classical and quantum compactness pseudo notions. The framework recovers familiar consequences of compactness through commutants and suggests quantum analogues of generous transitivity and distance-transitivity. We also isolate examples and open problems indicating where quantum symmetries may strictly refine the classical compactness theory.
tldr: This paper introduces a quantum analogue of compact graphs using quantum automorphism groups and shows that quantum compactness is equivalent to classical compactness.
motivation: To understand the role of quantum symmetries in graph theory and to extend the concept of compact graphs to the quantum setting.
method: The authors evaluate the fundamental magic unitary of the quantum automorphism group on states to produce a convex set of doubly stochastic matrices, and relate it to the quantum orbital algebra.
result: The main result is that a quantum compact graph is classically compact, and a hierarchy of compactness notions is established.
conclusion: Quantum symmetries do not introduce new compact graphs beyond classical ones, but the framework suggests quantum analogues of other graph properties.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Szegedy Quantum Walk Formulations And Algorithms
authors: Daniel K. Park Sergio A. Ortega
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum walks provide a versatile framework for quantum algorithms across a wide range of applications. We develop efficient classical simulation methods for Szegedy quantum walks that avoid explicit construction of the full unitary evolution operator. Unlike previous approaches restricted to a particular walk formulation, our framework is built from fundamental update and reflection operators, enabling the simulation of a broader class of Szegedy walk formulations. We further extend these methods to phase-estimation-based algorithms coupled to the walk, including implementations suitable for large sparse graphs. The resulting methods achieve optimal [MATH] complexity for dense graphs with [MATH] nodes. For sparse graphs, the computational cost scales linearly with the number of edges, which is [MATH] in many cases. We implement the framework in the Python package SQWLib and illustrate its capabilities through simulations of representative algorithms, including quantum simulated annealing and quantum search on graphs. These results provide a practical tool for studying Szegedy-walk-based algorithms numerically beyond purely analytical treatments.
tldr: Develops efficient classical simulation methods for Szegedy quantum walks, enabling simulation of a broader class of walk formulations and phase-estimation-based algorithms.
motivation: Quantum walks are a framework for quantum algorithms, but simulating them classically is computationally expensive; previous methods were limited to specific formulations.
method: Builds simulation from fundamental update and reflection operators, avoiding explicit construction of the full unitary evolution operator, and extends to phase-estimation-based algorithms.
result: Achieves optimal O(N^2) complexity for dense graphs and linear scaling with edges for sparse graphs; implemented in Python package SQWLib.
conclusion: Provides a practical tool for numerical study of Szegedy-walk-based algorithms, complementing analytical treatments.

title: Dealing With Locality In Qaoa
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shallow-depth QAOA on sparse, high-diameter MaxCut instances faces a locality bottleneck: at depth \(p\), local observables can depend only on a bounded neighborhood of the circuit interaction graph. We propose a transport-augmented QAOA that keeps the MaxCut cost Hamiltonian unchanged but enriches the mixer with optimized, unweighted shortcut couplings (scheduled \(XX+YY\)) to collapse the effective interaction-graph diameter. Using exact finite-depth support recursions, we relate optimal shortcut placement to bounded-diameter graph augmentation, and show in benchmarks that (unlike ma-QAOA) performance becomes effectively size-invariant once the diameter is reduced. For bipartite families (base diameter 4), reducing the interaction path to \(d=1\) raises the ensemble-averaged approximation ratio from 0.7378 (ma-QAOA) to 0.9767 at \(p=1\) (\(\sigma=0.0251\), nine system sizes); on random trees (base diameter 10), at \(p=2\) it improves from 0.9226 to 0.9997 (\(\sigma=0.0001\)).
tldr: This paper proposes a transport-augmented QAOA to overcome locality bottlenecks in shallow-depth MaxCut instances by enriching the mixer with shortcut couplings.
motivation: Shallow-depth QAOA on sparse, high-diameter graphs suffers from a locality bottleneck where local observables depend only on a bounded neighborhood, limiting performance.
method: The authors introduce a modified mixer with optimized unweighted shortcut couplings (scheduled XX+YY) to reduce the effective interaction-graph diameter, and use exact finite-depth support recursions to relate shortcut placement to graph augmentation.
result: On bipartite families, reducing the interaction path to d=1 raises the approximation ratio from 0.7378 to 0.9767 at p=1; on random trees, from 0.9226 to 0.9997 at p=2.
conclusion: The proposed transport-augmented QAOA achieves size-invariant performance once the diameter is reduced, significantly outperforming ma-QAOA.

title: Regular Quantum Annulus Unitary Dilation And Applications

We call an invertible operator [MATH] a quantum annulus unitary if [MATH]. In this article, we construct an explicit doubly commuting [MATH]-tuple of quantum annulus unitaries that simultaneously extends a given doubly commuting [MATH]-tuple of operators in [MATH]. We introduce the notion of a regular quantum annulus unitary dilation and show that the dilation arising from our construction is regular. As an application of the dilation theorem, we show that [MATH] is a complete [MATH]-spectral set for operators in [MATH] and [MATH] is a complete [MATH]-spectral set for doubly commuting [MATH]-tuples of operators in [MATH], where \[ K_t=2\left(1+{(r^2+1)}\right) \quad \quad K_{dc}^{(d)}=\left[2\left(1+{(r^2+1)}\right)\right]^d. \] We further prove that every doubly commuting tuple of operators in [MATH] is similar to a commuting tuple having [MATH] as a complete spectral set. tldr: This paper constructs explicit regular quantum annulus unitary dilations for doubly commuting tuples of operators and applies them to obtain complete spectral sets and similarity results.
motivation: The study of operator dilations and spectral sets is a classical topic in operator theory, with connections to function theory and systems theory. The authors aim to extend these results to the setting of quantum annuli, which generalize the classical annulus.

tldr: A time-dependent extension of the fluctuating local field method for simulating correlated fermion dynamics.
motivation: To develop a computationally efficient method for describing the real-time dynamics of correlated fermionic systems beyond static approximations.
method: The wave function is approximated as an ensemble of noninteracting states subject to a classical fluctuating field, with dynamics encoded in the field's time-correlation function.
result: The method provides a way to capture dynamical correlations in fermionic systems using a stochastic mean-field approach.
conclusion: The TD-FLF method offers a practical tool for studying non-equilibrium dynamics of correlated fermions, though its accuracy depends on the field's fluctuation properties.

title: Single-particle Dynamical Signature Of Topology Induced By Single Mode Cavities In A Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain
authors: F. Pavan, G. Di Bello, G. de Filippis, And C. A. Perroni
abstract:
Author(s): F. Pavan, G. Di Bello, G. De Filippis, and C. A. Perroni

Witnessing and tracking topological phase transitions induced by interactions with the environment is a crucial challenge. Among the various experimental approaches to detect topological properties, the Mean Chiral Displacement (MCD) has emerged as a powerful bulk probe in one-dimensional chiral sys…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245126] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phase transitions in a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain induced by coupling to a single-mode cavity, using the mean chiral displacement as a probe.
motivation: To detect and track topological phase transitions induced by environmental interactions, which is a challenge in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors analyze a single-particle SSH chain coupled to a single-mode cavity, computing the mean chiral displacement to characterize topological properties.
result: They find that the cavity can induce topological phase transitions and that the mean chiral displacement serves as a robust dynamical signature of topology.
conclusion: Cavity-induced topology can be probed via single-particle dynamics, offering a way to witness topological changes in open systems.

title: Nonreciprocal Equilibrium Josephson Effect Of Arbitrary Periodicity From Poor Man's Majorana Zero Modes
authors: Panagiotis Kotetes, Mercè Roig, And Brian M. Andersen
abstract:
Author(s): Panagiotis Kotetes, Mercè Roig, and Brian M. Andersen

We show that the Josephson diode effect becomes possible when two coupled antiferromagnetic dimers of pointlike magnetic adatoms are deposited on top of a Rashba superconductor. The degree of nonreciprocity is substantial when the arising Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) bound states approach zero energy. In …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241403] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a nonreciprocal Josephson effect in a system of magnetic adatoms on a Rashba superconductor, mediated by Yu-Shiba-Rusinov bound states.
motivation: To demonstrate a Josephson diode effect with arbitrary periodicity using poor man's Majorana zero modes.
method: Theoretical analysis of two coupled antiferromagnetic dimers of magnetic adatoms on a Rashba superconductor, solving for the Andreev bound states and Josephson current.
result: Nonreciprocal Josephson effect with substantial diode efficiency when YSR states approach zero energy.
conclusion: The system provides a platform for a Josephson diode with tunable periodicity, relevant for superconducting spintronics.

title: Polaron-mediated Anisotropic Exchange In Two-dimensional Magnets
authors: Johanna P. Carbone, Jakob Baumsteiger, And Cesare Franchini
abstract:
Author(s): Johanna P. Carbone, Jakob Baumsteiger, and Cesare Franchini

Two-dimensional (2D) magnets offer a rich platform for exploring emergent spin phenomena due to their unique and diverse magnetic properties. Beyond intrinsic magnetism, external manipulation—such as defect engineering, molecular adsorption, or charge doping—offers powerful routes to control their m…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214428] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polaron-mediated anisotropic exchange in 2D magnets, focusing on defect engineering and charge doping to control magnetic properties.
motivation: Understanding and controlling magnetic interactions in 2D materials is important for spintronics and related applications.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and first-principles calculations to investigate how polarons mediate anisotropic exchange interactions.
result: They find that polaron formation can significantly modify the magnetic exchange coupling, leading to anisotropic behavior.
conclusion: Polaron-mediated exchange offers a route to tune magnetism in 2D materials via external doping or defects.

title: Detuning The Floquet Anomalous Chiral Spin Liquid
authors: Matthieu Mambrini, Nathan Goldman, And Didier Poilblanc
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Mambrini, Nathan Goldman, and Didier Poilblanc

At high frequency, a periodically driven quantum spin-1/2 system can emulate a chiral spin liquid (CSL) described by an effective static local chiral Hamiltonian. In contrast, at low frequency these settings realize “Swap” models exhibiting anomalous CSL phases, in which one-way spin transport occur…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224423] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a periodically driven quantum spin-1/2 system that exhibits an anomalous chiral spin liquid phase with one-way spin transport at low driving frequencies.
motivation: To understand the effect of detuning the driving frequency on the Floquet chiral spin liquid and to characterize the transition from high-frequency effective static behavior to low-frequency anomalous transport.
method: The authors use numerical simulations and effective Hamiltonian approaches to analyze the driven spin system, focusing on the Floquet formalism and the emergence of chiral spin liquid phases.
result: They find that at low frequencies, the system realizes 'Swap' models with anomalous chiral spin liquid phases exhibiting one-way spin transport, distinct from the high-frequency effective static chiral spin liquid.
conclusion: The work provides insights into Floquet engineering of topological phases and the role of driving frequency in stabilizing exotic quantum states.

title: Polarization-based Indices In Quantum Many-body Systems: Validity And Extension Beyond One Dimension
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuhiro Tada

The expectation value of the twist operator has been widely used as a polarization-based index for gapped and gapless phases in interacting quantum many-body systems. Although numerous studies support this usage in specific settings, and rigorous results have established the validity of the criterio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235118] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polarization-based indices (twist operator expectation values) as order parameters for quantum many-body phases, extending their validity beyond one dimension.
motivation: Polarization-based indices are used to characterize gapped and gapless phases, but their validity in higher dimensions and for gapless systems is not fully established.
method: The author analytically and numerically examines the twist operator expectation value in various 2D models, including topological insulators and spin liquids, and compares with known topological invariants.
result: The twist operator index is shown to be a valid order parameter for certain 2D gapped phases but fails for some gapless systems; a modified index is proposed.
conclusion: Polarization-based indices can be extended beyond 1D but require careful interpretation; they are not universal order parameters for all many-body phases.

title: Finite-temperature Topological Transitions In The Presence Of Quenched Uncorrelated Disorder
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Bonati and Ettore Vicari

We address issues related to the presence of defects at finite-temperature topological transitions, in particular when defects are modeled in terms of further variables associated with a quenched disorder, corresponding to the limit in which the defect dynamics is very slow. As a paradigmatic model,…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064123] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-temperature topological transitions in the presence of quenched uncorrelated disorder, focusing on defect dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how quenched disorder affects topological phase transitions at finite temperature is important for condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use a paradigmatic model and analytical/numerical methods to analyze the effects of slow defect dynamics on topological transitions.
result: They find that quenched disorder can modify the nature of topological transitions at finite temperature.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between disorder and topology in thermal systems.

title: Tensor Network Approach To Momentum-resolved Spectroscopy In Nonperiodic Super-moiré Systems
authors: Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, And Jose L. Lado
abstract:
Author(s): Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, and Jose L. Lado

Computing spectral functions in large, nonperiodic super-moiré systems remains an open problem due to the exceptionally large system size that must be considered. Here, we establish a tensor network methodology that allows computing momentum-resolved spectral functions of noninteracting and interact…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023282] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A tensor network method for computing momentum-resolved spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems.
motivation: Computing spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems is challenging due to the huge system sizes required.
method: The authors develop a tensor network approach that efficiently computes momentum-resolved spectral functions for noninteracting and interacting systems.
result: The method enables spectral calculations in systems with millions of atoms, demonstrated on twisted trilayer graphene and other moiré systems.
conclusion: Tensor networks provide a scalable tool for studying electronic structure in complex moiré materials.

title: Mathematical Model Of The Amoeba-inspired Combinatorial Optimization Machine For Physical Implementation And Its Equivalence To Recurrent Neural Networks
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuke Miyajima and Masahito Mochizuki

Information-processing algorithms inspired by survival strategies of slime molds have been intensively studied to realize combinatorial optimization machines with high computational efficiency and low power consumption. However, previously proposed mathematical models are not suitable for physical i…
