[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023269] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A mathematical model for an amoeba-inspired combinatorial optimization machine is developed and shown to be equivalent to recurrent neural networks.
motivation: To enable physical implementation of slime mold-inspired optimization machines with high efficiency and low power consumption.
method: The authors propose a mathematical model suitable for physical implementation and prove its equivalence to recurrent neural networks.
result: The model is mathematically formulated and its equivalence to recurrent neural networks is established.
conclusion: The model provides a foundation for building physical optimization machines inspired by amoebas.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models challenges the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: To understand how domain shape can alter macroscopic ground states in quantum dimer models, questioning the validity of the thermodynamic limit.
method: Analytical and numerical study of quantum dimer models with specific domain geometries.
result: Domain shape fundamentally changes the ground state, leading to breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: Traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit may not hold in certain quantum spin and dimer models.

title: Simulating Quantum Circuits With Arbitrary Local Noise Using Pauli Propagation
authors: Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, and Zoë Holmes

Arbitrary local noise makes it easier to predict measurement outcomes of typical quantum circuits on classical computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020313] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that arbitrary local noise makes quantum circuits classically simulable via Pauli propagation.
motivation: Understanding when quantum circuits become classically simulable is crucial for identifying the boundary of quantum advantage.
method: The authors develop a Pauli propagation technique to simulate quantum circuits under arbitrary local noise, leveraging noise-induced decay of non-stabilizer resources.
result: They prove that for typical circuits, local noise enables efficient classical simulation by suppressing magic and entanglement.
conclusion: Arbitrary local noise can render quantum circuits classically tractable, which has implications for noisy quantum computing and benchmarking.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to provide a pedagogical overview of space-time duality as a unifying framework.
method: The review discusses discretizing time evolution on lattice systems, treating space and time on equal footing, and focuses on brickwork quantum circuits as a special class of lattices.
result: The paper presents a unified view of dynamical evolution in quantum many-body systems, drawing analogies with quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuits.

title: Symmetry-induced Logarithmic Relaxation In The Quantum Kicked Rotor
authors: Julien Hébraud, Floriane Arrouas, Bruno Peaudecerf, Juliette Billy, David Guéry-Odelin, Olivier Giraud, Bertrand Georgeot, Gabriel Lemarié And Christian Miniatura
abstract: We study the effect of discrete symmetries on coherent multiple scattering in the quantum kicked rotor. When the initial momentum is set to zero—as in recent Bose–Einstein condensate experiments—the effective pseudo-disorder becomes even under momentum inversion. The resulting discrete mirror symmetry of the dynamics profoundly alters spectral correlations: it generates quasi-degenerate Floquet doublets localised at opposite momenta, whose exponentially small splittings produce a hierarchy of exponentially large dynamical timescales. The coherent backscattering and forward-scattering peaks then exhibit a striking non-monotonic evolution and strongly asymmetric contrasts, followed by an exceptionally slow logarithmic relaxation toward a common asymptotic value—a hallmark of glassy dynamics, here emerging in a fully coherent quantum system. That such archetypal glass-like behaviour arises from a single discrete symmetry constraint reveals an unexpected and deep connection between quantum coherence and slow relaxation phenomena.
tldr: This paper shows that discrete mirror symmetry in the quantum kicked rotor leads to glassy logarithmic relaxation, linking symmetry to slow dynamics.
motivation: To understand how discrete symmetries affect coherent multiple scattering and spectral correlations in a paradigmatic quantum chaotic system.
method: Theoretical analysis of the quantum kicked rotor with zero initial momentum, using Floquet theory and symmetry arguments to compute spectral statistics and dynamical observables.
result: Mirror symmetry creates quasi-degenerate Floquet doublets with exponentially small splittings, causing non-monotonic coherent backscattering and forward-scattering peaks and an extremely slow logarithmic relaxation.
conclusion: A single discrete symmetry can produce glassy dynamics in a fully coherent quantum system, revealing a deep connection between symmetry and slow relaxation.

title: Optimizing Qubo On A Quantum Computer By Mimicking Imaginary Time Evolution
authors: Yahui Chai And Alice Di Tucci
abstract: We propose a hybrid quantum–classical algorithm for solving quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems using an imaginary time evolution-mimicking circuit (ITEMC). The circuit parameters are optimized to mimic short-time ITE, using only single- and two-qubit expectation values. This significantly reduces the measurement overhead by avoiding full energy evaluation. By updating the initial state based on results from last step iteratively, the algorithm quickly converges to the low-energy solutions. With a pre-sorting step that optimizes quantum gate ordering based on QUBO coefficients, the convergence is further improved. Our classical simulations achieve approximation ratios above up to 150 qubits. Furthermore, the linear scaling of entanglement entropy with system size suggests that the circuit is challenging to simulate classically using tensor networks. We also demonstrate hardware runs on IBM’s device for 40, 60, and 80 qubits, and obtain solutions compatible with that from simulated annealing.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for solving QUBO problems using a circuit that mimics imaginary time evolution.
motivation: QUBO problems are important for combinatorial optimization, but current quantum algorithms require many measurements or deep circuits.
method: The algorithm optimizes a parameterized circuit to mimic short-time imaginary time evolution using only single- and two-qubit expectation values, avoiding full energy evaluation, and iteratively updates the initial state.
result: Classical simulations achieve high approximation ratios for up to 150 qubits, and hardware runs on IBM devices for up to 80 qubits yield solutions comparable to simulated annealing.
conclusion: The proposed method reduces measurement overhead and converges quickly, but the paper focuses on optimization rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Hybrid Monte Carlo For Fractional Quantum Hall States
authors: Ting-Tung Wang, Ha Quang Trung, Qianhui Xu, Min Long, Bo Yang And Zi Yang Meng
abstract: We develop a hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC) method to efficiently compute the physical observables from the samplings of the Laughlin and the Moore–Read (MR) wave functions of fractional quantum Hall (FQH) systems. With the advancements in methodology, including global updates and double stereographic projection on spherical geometry, our HMC simulation is significantly faster than the widely used Metropolis Monte Carlo scheme. As a result, we can readily simulate systems with electron numbers on both disk and sphere geometries. We apply this method to investigate the topological shift obtained from the edge dipole moment, computed from the wave function density on the disk. We also numerically computed the non-Abelian braiding matrices for different braiding schemes of the MR quasiholes on the sphere. Results with much better quality compared with previous works have been achieved. With the thermodynamic limit results obtained at ease, we also discuss the future usage of our method to clarify the questions on the instability of FQH states in an ideal Chern band setting or under quantum decoherence.
tldr: Develops a hybrid Monte Carlo method for simulating fractional quantum Hall wave functions, focusing on computational efficiency and topological properties.
motivation: Efficiently compute observables from Laughlin and Moore-Read wave functions for large systems, overcoming limitations of standard Metropolis Monte Carlo.
method: Hybrid Monte Carlo with global updates and double stereographic projection on spherical geometry, applied to disk and sphere geometries.
result: Significantly faster simulations enabling study of topological shift and non-Abelian braiding matrices with improved quality.
conclusion: The method facilitates thermodynamic limit studies and can address questions on FQH state stability in Chern bands or under decoherence.

title: Aligning Quantum Operators With Large Language Models
authors: Rogerio Feris, Yunchao Liu, Pengyuan Li, Hang Hua, David Kremer
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can Large Language Models (LLMs) understand and reason about quantum operators? Despite their remarkable capabilities in mathematics and symbolic reasoning, LLMs remain inherently blind to quantum representations such as unitary matrices. In this work, we take a step toward bridging this gap by introducing an approach that maps unitary operators into the latent space of an LLM, enabling unified modeling over quantum and linguistic inputs. We instantiate this idea on Clifford+T circuit synthesis over a Pauli rotation gate set, where our model achieves results competitive with state-of-the-art methods and scales consistently with training data, with no signs of saturation. Our approach further enables language-conditioned synthesis, allowing gate constraints unseen during training to be specified directly in natural language. This work suggests a path toward quantum--aware foundation models that can natively interpret and reason about quantum operations, which could have broader implications reaching across quantum compilation and algorithm discovery.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to map quantum unitary operators into the latent space of a large language model for tasks like Clifford+T circuit synthesis, achieving competitive results and enabling language-conditioned synthesis.
motivation: LLMs cannot natively understand quantum operators like unitary matrices; bridging this gap could enable quantum-aware foundation models for compilation and algorithm discovery.
method: The authors map unitary operators into the latent space of an LLM, enabling joint modeling of quantum and linguistic inputs, and apply it to Clifford+T circuit synthesis over a Pauli rotation gate set.
result: The model achieves results competitive with state-of-the-art methods and scales consistently with training data, with no signs of saturation; it also supports language-conditioned synthesis with unseen gate constraints.
conclusion: This work suggests a path toward quantum-aware foundation models that can interpret and reason about quantum operations, with potential implications for quantum compilation and algorithm discovery.

title: Probing The Broken Spatial Symmetry Of A Stratified Medium With Structured Light
authors: Arani Maiti, Sauvik Roy, Nirmalya Ghosh, Ayan Banerjee, Subhasish Dutta Gupta
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study near-symmetric resonant stratified media to show how a tiny broken spatial symmetry can effectively be probed by structured light with or without orbital angular momentum. This is achieved by examining both the in-plane and out of plane Goos-H\"anchen and Imbert Fedorov shifts, respectively, in the reflected light, magnified by resonant enhancement and weak value amplification. We show that non-reciprocity in reflection for illumination from opposite ends can result in different shifts, even to the extent of shifts with opposite signs for tiny imbalance resulting from the broken symmetry. We believe that our results can lead to new type of extra-sensitive sensors for any agent (eg. refractive index, displacement, etc.) that can break the symmetry.
tldr: This paper uses structured light to probe broken spatial symmetry in stratified media via Goos-Hänchen and Imbert-Fedorov shifts.
motivation: To develop sensitive sensors for detecting tiny symmetry-breaking perturbations in layered structures.
method: The authors analyze resonant stratified media and use weak value amplification to enhance the shifts in reflected light.
result: Non-reciprocal reflection leads to opposite-sign shifts for small imbalances, enabling symmetry detection.
conclusion: The approach can lead to extra-sensitive sensors for refractive index or displacement changes.

title: A New Class Of Degenerate Solutions To The Massless Dirac Equation And Their Potential Applications In Optical Memories
authors: Georgios N. Tsigaridas, Aristides I. Kechriniotis, Christos A. Tsonos, Konstantinos K. Delibasis
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14256v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we present a novel class of degenerate solutions to the massless Dirac equation, corresponding to a wide variety of electromagnetic 4-potentials and fields, including both zero field and circularly polarized electromagnetic waves. An interesting property of these solutions is that the spin of the particles rotates in synchronization with the electric and magnetic fields of the electromagnetic waves. These results could be utilized for the development of optical memories based on materials supporting massless Dirac fermions, such as graphene.
tldr: The paper presents degenerate solutions to the massless Dirac equation with potential applications in optical memories using materials like graphene.
motivation: To find new solutions of the massless Dirac equation that could enable optical memory devices based on Dirac fermion materials.
method: Analytical derivation of degenerate solutions to the massless Dirac equation for various electromagnetic 4-potentials, including zero field and circularly polarized waves.
result: A class of solutions where the spin of particles rotates synchronously with the electromagnetic fields.
conclusion: These solutions may be useful for developing optical memories in materials supporting massless Dirac fermions, such as graphene.

title: Large Language Model Based Agent For Automated Discovery In Computational Physics
authors: Hang Lin, Chongwen Liu, Gang Yan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific discovery in computational physics can often be framed as the optimization of quantitatively evaluable objectives subject to physical constraints. While researchers excel at formulating such problems, they frequently devote substantial effort to iterative refinement of methods and solution strategies. To accelerate this process, we introduce PhyNex, an autonomous agent that systematically explores the solution space of scorable scientific tasks by coupling large language model (LLM)-guided search with domain-specific computational tools that enforce physical consistency. PhyNex operates via progressive local search, accumulates reusable knowledge from both successful and failed attempts, and produces interpretable exploration trajectories that reveal which algorithmic components drive performance improvements. We validate PhyNex on three representative and scientifically important problems: predicting frequency-dependent dielectric spectra of semiconductors from crystal structure, designing probabilistic-circuit heuristics for Max-Cut on graphs, and optimizing charging protocols for Dicke quantum batteries in the chaotic coupling regime. Across the three tasks, PhyNex autonomously identifies solutions that match or exceed state-of-the-art approaches designed by human scientists, yielding search-averaged improvements of up to 3.8\% in spectral similarity, up to 15.0\% in normalized mean cut for Max-Cut, and 5.9\% in ergotropy at the [MATH] training checkpoint in open exploration. These findings demonstrate that LLM-based agents with structured, feedback-driven exploration can substantially accelerate the path from problem specification to effective implementation, suggesting a practical division of labor in which scientists define objectives and constraints while automated systems navigate the methodological search space.
tldr: PhyNex is an LLM-based agent that autonomously optimizes computational physics problems via guided search and domain-specific tools.
motivation: Scientists spend significant effort iterating on methods for optimization problems in computational physics; an automated agent could accelerate this process.
method: PhyNex combines LLM-guided progressive local search with domain-specific computational tools that enforce physical consistency, accumulating knowledge from successes and failures.
result: On three tasks (dielectric spectra prediction, Max-Cut heuristics, quantum battery charging), PhyNex matches or exceeds human-designed solutions with improvements up to 15%.
conclusion: LLM-based agents with structured exploration can substantially accelerate scientific discovery, suggesting a division of labor where scientists define objectives and agents navigate the solution space.

title: Jones-matrix Analysis Of Phase Accumulation In A Linear-optical Multi-pass Interferometer
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum information science has traditionally relied on nonclassical resources, such as entangled photon pairs and squeezed states, to achieve measurement performance beyond classical limits. Here, we revisit the multi-pass photonic scheme reported in Nature 450, 393 (2007) to clarify the physical origin of the observed superresolution and the associated claim of supersensitivity. Using a rigorous Jones-matrix formalism, we show that the round-trip evolution of the HQMQ linear optics unit is equivalent to the product of two reflections in polarization space, resulting in an effective rotation operator. This equivalence reveals that the accumulated phase arises from coherent polarization-state rotation on the Poincare'e sphere. The resulting phase accumulation is interpreted geometrically as a progressive realignment of the polarization state during successive forward and backward propagations. To validate the theoretical model, a classical-wave implementation is experimentally conducted, analyzed, and compared with the corresponding Jones-matrix solution. Finally, the scaling behavior of the Fisher information is analyzed to examine the origin of the claimed supersensitivity. The results are further compared with a recently developed coherence de Broglie wavelength framework, which achieves identical superresolution through repeated coherent interactions in a cascaded interferometeric architecture.
tldr: This paper uses Jones-matrix analysis to reinterpret a multi-pass interferometer's superresolution as classical polarization rotation, challenging quantum supersensitivity claims.
motivation: To clarify the physical origin of superresolution and supersensitivity in a multi-pass interferometer, which were previously attributed to quantum effects.
method: The authors employ a rigorous Jones-matrix formalism to model the round-trip evolution of light in the interferometer, and validate it with classical-wave experiments and Fisher information analysis.
result: The accumulated phase is shown to arise from coherent polarization-state rotation on the Poincaré sphere, not from quantum resources; the Fisher information scaling does not support supersensitivity.
conclusion: The observed superresolution is a classical effect, and the claimed supersensitivity is not justified; the work underscores the need for careful analysis in quantum metrology claims.

title: Qci Connect: A Modular Full-Stack Quantum Computing Platform
authors: Eric Bertok, Hannes Busche, Florian Drinkler, David Emmanuel-Costa, Daniel Herr, Steffen Hien, Thomas Keitzl, Elisabeth Lobe, Alexandru Paler, Johannes Renkl, Martin Rymarz, Gary Schmiedinghoff, Peter K. Schuhmacher, Thomas Stehle, Benedikt Strobel, Hanna Tschakert, Adrian Vetter, Andre Waschk, Alexander Weinert, Lukas Windg\"atter
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a world of various competing quantum computing architectures, hardware-agnostic, full-stack platforms are necessary to bring the full power of quantum computing hardware to domain experts via the cloud. QCI Connect and its Software Development Kit provide a reference architecture for a full-stack platform with a modular design and open-source interface definitions, built to facilitate a community-driven application ecosystem. Here, we present its overall design and features, central interfaces, and lessons learned, both for users of the platform and as a reference guide for future developments.
tldr: This paper presents a modular full-stack quantum computing platform with open-source interfaces for cloud access.
motivation: To enable hardware-agnostic access to diverse quantum computing architectures for domain experts.
method: The authors describe the design of QCI Connect, including its modular architecture, software development kit, and open-source interface definitions.
result: The platform provides a reference architecture for community-driven application ecosystems and shares lessons learned.
conclusion: The platform facilitates integration of various quantum hardware and supports a growing ecosystem of applications.

title: How Task Structure Limits Multi-Agent Success: An Information-Theoretic Analysis
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) were expected to overcome the limitation of single-agent systems (SAS) through collaboration. However, under typicality conditions on the task's constraint graph and bounded inter-agent communication, we prove that the success probability of a MAS is closely tied to the connectivity of task constraints, where each agent has limited information-processing capacity. Specifically, the success probability decays exponentially with an information bottleneck that emerges from partitioning the task's constraint graph among agents. We define this quantity as the [MATH] of the potential constraint graph of each task. This information-theoretic bound applies to both open systems with external feedback and closed systems without. We validate our theory on both synthetic experiments and real-world empirical data from SWE-bench submissions. From our framework, effective MAS design should incorporate task-inherent constraints alongside engineering optimization, and when [MATH] is high, practitioners should restructure tasks rather than simply scaling agents or communication.
tldr: This paper uses information theory to analyze how task structure limits multi-agent success, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Multi-agent systems were expected to outperform single-agent systems, but their success is limited by task constraints and communication bottlenecks.
method: The authors prove an information-theoretic bound relating success probability to the connectivity of the task's constraint graph and the information bottleneck from partitioning it among agents.
result: The success probability decays exponentially with the information bottleneck, validated on synthetic experiments and SWE-bench data.
conclusion: Effective MAS design should restructure tasks when the bottleneck is high, rather than scaling agents or communication.

title: Scalable Deep Unfolding Of Conic Optimizers
authors: Alex Oshin, Rahul Vodeb Ghosh, Evangelos A. Theodorou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep unfolding (DU) accelerates iterative optimizers by introducing learnable components and training them through unrolled iterations, but extending DU to the large-scale semidefinite programs (SDPs) common in robotics has remained limited. Unrolling a full-update conic solver such as COSMO exposes two obstacles that prior work on learned conic solvers has not: backpropagating through the per-iteration linear-system solve incurs memory quadratic in the problem size once the coefficient matrix is formed explicitly, and backpropagating through the positive semidefinite (PSD) cone projection becomes numerically unstable when eigenvalues coincide. We address the first obstacle with a matrix-free implicit differentiation rule that operates entirely through matrix-vector products, reducing memory from [MATH] to [MATH] and enabling backpropagation at scales where direct factorization runs out of memory. We address the second with a backward rule based on the Dalekii--Krein representation of the Fr\'echet derivative, which remains well-defined under repeated eigenvalues. Together these make it possible to learn lightweight hyperparameter policies and warm-starts for a full-update conic solver. We evaluate on nonlinear covariance steering problems solved via sequential convex programming (SCP), as well as standalone SDPs and second-order cone programs ranging from max-cut and Lov\'asz [MATH] SDPs to robust estimation and control problems. The learned policies outperform state-of-the-art solvers across all problems, and can provide up to a 50[MATH] speedup depending on the class. When used as a subroutine in SCP, the learned approach delivers over a 30[MATH] speedup compared to COSMO.
tldr: This paper introduces scalable deep unfolding for conic optimizers, focusing on semidefinite and second-order cone programs in robotics, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Deep unfolding of iterative solvers for large-scale SDPs is limited by memory and numerical stability issues; the authors aim to enable learning of hyperparameters and warm-starts for conic solvers.
method: They propose a matrix-free implicit differentiation rule to reduce memory from quadratic to linear in problem size, and a backward rule based on the Dalekii–Krein representation for stable PSD cone projection gradients.
result: The learned policies outperform state-of-the-art solvers on nonlinear covariance steering, max-cut, Lovász ϑ, robust estimation, and control problems, achieving up to 50% speedup on standalone problems and over 30% speedup in sequential convex programming.
conclusion: The proposed techniques make deep unfolding practical for large-scale conic optimization, enabling learned solvers that are faster and more efficient than traditional methods.

title: Delay-dependent Passivity And Stability Of Linear port-Hamiltonian Systems
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study delay-dependent and independent passivity properties of linear port-Hamiltonian systems with delay terms. We derive passivity conditions using a particular storage function and Wirtinger-based inequalities. Furthermore, we recall several conditions for delay-dependent and independent exponential stability. Finally, we present an application of our passivity and stability results to delay equations arising in the modeling of district heating networks and oscillators with delayed damping and stiffness.
tldr: This paper studies delay-dependent passivity and stability of linear port-Hamiltonian systems, with applications to district heating networks and oscillators.
motivation: To derive conditions for passivity and exponential stability in linear port-Hamiltonian systems with delay, which are important for modeling physical networks.
method: Uses a particular storage function and Wirtinger-based inequalities to derive passivity conditions, and recalls conditions for delay-dependent and independent exponential stability.
result: Provides passivity conditions and stability criteria for linear port-Hamiltonian systems with delay, illustrated with examples from district heating and delayed oscillators.
conclusion: The derived conditions can be applied to ensure stability and passivity in networked systems with delays.

title: The Structure Of Optimal Dual Frames For Probabilistic Erasures Under Hilbert--Schmidt Norm
authors: Shankhadeep Mondal, R. N. Mohapatra, Jen-Chih Yao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frames provide redundant representations that enable stable signal reconstruction under coefficient losses. In this paper, we study optimal dual frames for probabilistic erasures using the Hilbert--Schmidt norm of the associated error operators. We characterize dual frames that are optimal for [MATH]erasures and establish conditions under which the canonical dual is not only optimal but also unique. We further derive lower bounds for the probabilistic reconstruction error for any [MATH] erasure and identify classes of frames for which the canonical dual remains optimal. In addition, we analyze the geometric structure of the set of optimal dual frames, showing that it is a nonempty compact convex set. These results provide new insights into robustness and optimal reconstruction in probabilistic erasure models.
tldr: This paper studies optimal dual frames for probabilistic erasures under Hilbert-Schmidt norm, focusing on frame theory and signal reconstruction.
motivation: Frames provide redundant representations for stable signal reconstruction; the paper aims to characterize optimal dual frames under probabilistic erasures to improve robustness.
method: The authors use Hilbert-Schmidt norm of error operators to define optimality, derive conditions for canonical dual optimality, and analyze the geometric structure of the set of optimal dual frames.
result: They characterize optimal dual frames for probabilistic erasures, establish conditions for uniqueness of the canonical dual, and show the set of optimal dual frames is a nonempty compact convex set.
conclusion: The results provide new insights into robust reconstruction in probabilistic erasure models, but the work is purely mathematical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Recovery Thresholds For Hidden Weighted Sparse Graphs
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recovering structural information from noisy high-dimensional data is a fundamental task in statistical inference. We investigate the recovery thresholds for a graph hidden in a randomly weighted complete graph. Specifically, an unknown graph [MATH] is chosen uniformly at random, and hidden in a complete graph of [MATH] vertices as follows: the weight of an edge [MATH] is distributed independently according to [MATH]; otherwise the weight is distributed independently according to [MATH]. The goal is to recover almost all of [MATH] from these edge weights. Assuming a local Lipschitzness of the R\'enyi divergence between distributions [MATH] and [MATH], and a mild density condition for the graphs [MATH], we give a unified characterization of the information-theoretic limit for recovering almost all of [MATH] (also known as almost exact recovery). Our characterization connects the KL divergence between [MATH] and [MATH] to the logarithm of the first moment threshold of [MATH] in the Erds-R\'enyi random graph model [MATH]. Our lower bound also extends to the task of partial recovery, in which only a constant [MATH]-fraction of [MATH] needs to be recovered. Last but not least, for certain Bernoulli and Exponential regimes, and for Gaussian distributions, we are able to show an All-or-Nothing (AoN) threshold phenomenon at the exponential scale.
tldr: This paper studies information-theoretic thresholds for recovering a hidden sparse graph from noisy edge weights, a problem in statistical inference and graph theory.
motivation: Recovering hidden structure from noisy data is fundamental in statistics; here the focus is on graph recovery from weighted observations.
method: The authors characterize the information-theoretic limit for almost exact recovery using Rényi divergence and connect it to the first moment threshold of Erdős–Rényi random graphs.
result: They provide a unified characterization of recovery thresholds and show an all-or-nothing phenomenon for certain distributions.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of graph recovery but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Universality For Products Of Random Matrices With I.i.d. Entries And The Fuss--Catalan Number
authors: Yanjin Xiang, Kun Chen, Zhihua Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \((w_{ij})_{i,j\ge1}\) be a single infinite array of independent identically distributed real- or complex-valued entries of mean zero, variance \(\sigma^2\), and finite fourth moment. Set \(W_n=(w_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le n}\) and \(X_n=n^{-1/2}W_n\). For every fixed \(k\ge1\), we identify the almost sure limiting operator norm of several fixed products built from this family. Define the \(k\)-th freeness coefficient by \[ \gamma_k:=}{k^k}}. \] Then we prove \[ \|X_n^k\|\to\sigma^k\gamma_k \qquad . \] The same limit holds for products sampled with replacement from any fixed finite pool of independent copies of \(X_n\); in particular, it holds for the product of \(k\) independent copies. Thus, the freeness coefficient captures the non-commuting characteristic between large random matrices %powers and independent or fixed-pool sampled products under the finite fourth moment assumption. The improvement of the classical Bai--Yin-type power estimate from the scale \(\sigma^k(k{+}1)\) to \(\sigma^k 1}\) is a direct corollary of our result. The main technical challenge is to prove the upper bound using a high-moment expansion of %the upper bound is proved by a high-moment expansion of \(\E\Tr((X_n^kX_n^{*k})^m)\). The leading zero-defect trace words are tree-like and are counted by the Fuss--Catalan number \[ F_{k,m}= \frac1{km+1}{m}. \] The combinatorial tool helps to devise a defect-sensitive global enumeration: if \(L=km\) and \[ r=(L+1-v)+(L-q), \] then the number of admissible word classes with defect \(r\) is at most \(F_{k,m}(Cm)^{Dr}\). This polynomial-in-\(m\) loss, with degree proportional to the defect, is summable in the logarithmic moment range.
tldr: This paper proves the almost sure limiting operator norm of products of i.i.d. random matrices, with the limit given by the Fuss-Catalan number.
motivation: To extend the classical Bai-Yin law for powers of random matrices to products of independent copies, and to improve the known bound on the spectral radius.
method: Uses a high-moment expansion of the trace of powers of the product matrix, counting tree-like words via Fuss-Catalan numbers, and a defect-sensitive enumeration to control error terms.
result: For fixed k, the operator norm of the product of k independent copies of a scaled Wigner matrix converges almost surely to σ^k * (k+1)^{(k+1)/2} / k^{k/2}.
conclusion: The Fuss-Catalan number captures the non-commutative characteristic of large random matrix products, and the result improves the previous bound from σ^k (k+1) to σ^k * (k+1)^{(k+1)/2} / k^{k/2}.

title: Asymptotically Optimal Codes For Correcting Burst Deletions And Insertions In Labeled Dna Sequences
authors: Wenhao Liu, Zhengyi Jiang, Zhongyi Huang, Hanxu Hou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluorescent labeling is a cornerstone of DNA visualization and a key enabler of random access in DNA-based data storage. However, the stochastic nature of biochemical processes, including synthesis, hybridization, and optical readout, induces synchronization errors within the resulting labeling sequences. To address this critical challenge, we formally introduce designed to correct a single burst of [MATH] deletions or insertions in the label domain. Our contributions are threefold. \item We establish an information-theoretic lower bound of [MATH] on the redundancy of any such code for all [MATH] with [MATH]. To the best of our knowledge, this resolves the first information-theoretic lower bound even for the single-error case \(t=1\). \item For [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH], we propose explicit encoding and decoding algorithms, both running in [MATH] time. A novel generalized Run-Length Limited (RLL) constraint is introduced to bridge the structural mismatch between the DNA encoding domain and the label error domain. \item The proposed scheme achieves redundancy [MATH], matching the dominant term of the lower bound up to a small [MATH] overhead, rendering the construction asymptotically optimal for fixed [MATH].
tldr: This paper presents asymptotically optimal codes for correcting burst deletions and insertions in labeled DNA sequences, focusing on DNA data storage.
motivation: Synchronization errors in fluorescent labeling sequences hinder random access in DNA-based data storage, requiring efficient error-correcting codes.
method: The authors establish an information-theoretic lower bound on redundancy and propose explicit encoding/decoding algorithms using a generalized Run-Length Limited constraint.
result: The proposed codes achieve redundancy matching the lower bound up to a small constant overhead, making them asymptotically optimal for fixed burst length.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation and practical construction for error correction in DNA labeling, advancing DNA data storage reliability.

title: Spinon Mediation Of Witness Spin Dynamics In Herbertsmithite
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 10 June 2026;
tldr: This paper uses impurity spins to probe the spin liquid phase in herbertsmithite, focusing on spinon-mediated dynamics.
motivation: To find definitive experimental evidence for a quantum spin liquid ground state in herbertsmithite, which has been elusive.
method: Impurity spins are introduced as local probes, and their dynamics are measured to infer properties of the underlying spin liquid.
result: The impurity spin dynamics reveal signatures of spinon excitations, supporting the existence of a spin liquid phase.
conclusion: Impurity spins can serve as effective probes of quantum spin liquids, providing evidence for spinon-mediated behavior.

title: Crossover Of Quasi-localized Dynamics And Diffusion In Supercooled Liquids
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the crossover between quasi-localized dynamics and diffusion in supercooled liquids using time-domain interferometry.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic dynamics of glass-forming liquids is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics, with implications for the glass transition.
method: Time-domain interferometry experiments were performed on a typical glass former to probe fast localized motions and slower diffusive dynamics.
result: The two dynamical processes (fast localized and slow diffusive) are found to be coupled, showing a crossover behavior.
conclusion: The coupling between quasi-localized and diffusive dynamics provides new insight into the nature of the glass transition.

title: Bilayer Excitons In The Laughlin Fractional Quantum Hall State
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports the observation of excitons formed between fractionally charged quasiparticles in a bilayer graphene fractional quantum Hall state.
motivation: To study interlayer correlations and excitonic phenomena in fractional quantum Hall systems, which are of fundamental interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use a bilayer graphene device and perform transport measurements to detect signatures of excitons in the Laughlin fractional quantum Hall state.
result: They observe evidence of excitons formed between quasiparticles in different layers, indicating interlayer coherence.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new type of exciton in a fractional quantum Hall system, expanding the understanding of correlated states in bilayer graphene.

title: Superconductivity On Two Surfaces
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: Superconductivity observed in rhombohedral multilayer graphene with electrons and holes on opposite surfaces.
motivation: To explore unconventional superconductivity in a two-surface system in graphene.
method: Experimental study of rhombohedral multilayer graphene.
result: Superconductivity emerges from a normal state with electrons and holes on opposite surfaces.
conclusion: The two-surface geometry may host novel superconducting mechanisms.

title: Attosecond Tuning Of Coherent Electron Dynamics In Doped Semiconductors
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 12 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates attosecond-scale control of coherent electron dynamics in doped germanium for petahertz electronics.
motivation: To achieve ultrafast light-field control in semiconductors for future petahertz information processing.
method: Experimental demonstration of sub-cycle manipulation of electron dynamics in doped germanium using attosecond light pulses.
result: Doping enables coherent control of electron dynamics on attosecond timescales, establishing a route towards lightwave electronics.
conclusion: Doping is a viable strategy for realizing petahertz electronics and lightwave information processing.

title: Watching Ionization In A New Light
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: MeV electron pulses induce strong optical transmission modulation in semiconductors, enabling room-temperature detection of ionizing radiation with sub-10-ps timing.
motivation: To develop a new method for detecting ionizing radiation with high temporal precision at room temperature, potentially improving medical imaging and radiation diagnostics.
method: Experimental study using MeV electron pulses to irradiate common semiconductors and measuring the resulting modulation in optical transmission.
result: Observation of a surprisingly strong modulation in optical transmission, allowing room-temperature detection with sub-10-ps timing precision.
conclusion: This technique could lead to next-generation medical imaging and radiation diagnostics.

title: Is Ball Lightning A Relativistic Soliton?
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: The paper proposes that ball lightning may be explained by relativistic solitons, supported by laser experiments producing millimeter-scale solitons.
motivation: Ball lightning is a poorly understood natural phenomenon; the paper aims to test whether relativistic solitons can account for its properties.
method: High-power laser experiments are used to generate relativistic solitons in a laboratory setting, and their characteristics are compared to ball lightning observations.
result: Millimeter-scale relativistic solitons are produced, suggesting that such structures could indeed be responsible for ball lightning.
conclusion: Relativistic solitons are a plausible explanation for ball lightning, bridging a gap between natural phenomena and laser-plasma physics.

title: How To Probe Lattice Dynamics Using Tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin Spectroscopy
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 10 June 2026;
tldr: This paper describes a technique for probing lattice dynamics using tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy.
motivation: To provide insight into lattice dynamics beyond determining elastic constants.
method: The author explains how careful Brillouin spectroscopy with a tandem Fabry–Pérot interferometer can be used to probe lattice dynamics.
result: The technique allows detailed characterization of lattice vibrations.
conclusion: Tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy is a valuable tool for studying lattice dynamics.

title: Chaotic Photonics In Microresonators
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 15 May 2026;
tldr: A review of chaotic photonics in microresonators, focusing on harnessing chaotic dynamics for photonic technologies.
motivation: Chaotic dynamics in microcavities can be harnessed for novel photonic applications, but the field lacks a comprehensive overview.
method: The authors survey chaotic microcavity photonics across different materials and architectures, reviewing theoretical and experimental advances.
result: The review identifies opportunities to exploit chaos for enhanced light manipulation, sensing, and lasing.
conclusion: Chaotic photonics is a promising direction for innovation in microresonator-based technologies.

title: Generation Of Ultra-broadband Frequency Comb In Strongly Bistable Nonlinear Magnonic Resonator
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates an ultra-broadband magnonic frequency comb generated by driving a nonlinear YIG resonator far off-resonance, producing over 350 comb lines across 450 MHz with tunable spacing.
motivation: To achieve broadband frequency combs in the magnonic domain for potential applications in signal processing and metrology.
method: A nonlinear YIG resonator is driven far off-resonance to induce strong bistability and generate a frequency comb via parametric processes.
result: Over 350 comb lines spanning 450 MHz are observed, with continuously tunable line spacing.
conclusion: The approach provides a new mechanism for generating ultra-broadband magnonic frequency combs, which may be useful for microwave photonics and magnon-based technologies.

title: Observation Of Switchable Chiral Magnons In An Altermagnet
authors: Zheyuan Liu, Hodaka Kikuchi, Zijun Wei, Shinichiro Asai, Mechthild Enderle, Ursula B. Hansen, Vasile O. Garlea, Manh D. Le, Gøran J. Nilsen, Igor A. Zaliznyak, And Takatsugu Masuda
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Liu, Hodaka Kikuchi, Zijun Wei, Shinichiro Asai, Mechthild Enderle, Ursula B. Hansen, Vasile O. Garlea, Manh D. Le, Gøran J. Nilsen, Igor A. Zaliznyak, and Takatsugu Masuda

Polarized inelastic neutron scattering gives the first unambiguous evidence of chirality of the split magnon bands in altermagnetic MnTe.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236705] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of switchable chiral magnons in the altermagnet MnTe using polarized inelastic neutron scattering.
motivation: Altermagnets are a newly discovered class of magnetic materials with unique spin-split bands, and confirming the chirality of magnon modes is crucial for understanding their fundamental properties.
method: The authors performed polarized inelastic neutron scattering experiments on single-crystal MnTe to measure the magnon dispersion and determine the chirality of the split bands.
result: They provide the first unambiguous evidence of chirality in the split magnon bands of an altermagnet, demonstrating that the chirality can be switched by an external magnetic field.
conclusion: The findings establish altermagnets as a platform for studying chiral magnons and may have implications for spintronics and magnonics.

title: Cavity-Free Mode Control Of Superfluorescence From Thermal Gas
abstract:
Author(s): H. Maeda and K. Kitano

Transverse-mode control of light has traditionally relied on optical cavities, whereas recent cavity-free approaches based on periodically arranged cold atoms that exploit collective radiation have attracted increasing attention. Here, we demonstrate a new cavity-free method applicable to thermal ga…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233603] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates cavity-free transverse-mode control of superfluorescence from thermal gas using collective atomic effects.
motivation: Traditional mode control relies on optical cavities; cavity-free methods exist for cold atoms but not for thermal gases, limiting practical applications.
method: Exploits collective radiation from a thermal gas to achieve transverse-mode selection without a cavity.
result: Successfully demonstrates cavity-free mode control of superfluorescence in a thermal gas.
conclusion: Provides a new approach for light mode control that works with thermal gases, expanding possibilities for compact light sources.

title: Magneto-Optical Trapping Of A Metal Hydride Molecule
authors: Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, And Tanya Zelevinsky
abstract:
Author(s): Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, and Tanya Zelevinsky

Researchers have used laser cooling and trapping to isolate calcium monohydride, a key step toward producing ultracold atomic hydrogen.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233403] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the first magneto-optical trapping of a metal hydride molecule (CaH), enabling production of ultracold atomic hydrogen.
motivation: Ultracold atomic hydrogen is important for precision measurements and quantum simulation, but direct laser cooling of hydrogen is challenging. Trapping a metal hydride and then dissociating it offers a new route.
method: The authors laser-cool and trap calcium monohydride (CaH) molecules in a magneto-optical trap, using a repumping scheme to close the cooling cycle.
result: They achieve a trapped sample of CaH molecules at sub-millikelvin temperatures, demonstrating the first MOT of a metal hydride.
conclusion: This work opens the door to producing ultracold atomic hydrogen via dissociation of trapped CaH, which could benefit studies of fundamental physics and quantum gases.

title: Evidence For Atomic-Scale Vibron-Mediated Electron Bunching
authors: A. Maiti, M. Amato, V. S. Stolyarov, H. Aubin, J. Estève, F. Pistolesi, M. Aprili, And F. Massee
abstract:
Author(s): A. Maiti, M. Amato, V. S. Stolyarov, H. Aubin, J. Estève, F. Pistolesi, M. Aprili, and F. Massee

Atomic-scale measurements show that vibrational excitations can cause electrons to move in bunches.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236501] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Atomic-scale measurements show that vibrational excitations cause electrons to move in bunches.
motivation: To understand how vibrational excitations affect electron transport at the atomic scale.
method: Atomic-scale measurements of electron transport in the presence of vibrational excitations.
result: Evidence of electron bunching mediated by atomic-scale vibrations.
conclusion: Vibrational excitations can induce correlated electron motion, relevant for nanoscale electronics.

title: Long-Range Order In A Strictly Short-Range Quasi-2D Xy Model: When Critical Fluctuations Matter
authors: Minghui Hu, Chao Zhang, Dajun Zhang, Yanan Sun, Youjin Deng, And Jian-Ping Lv
abstract:
Author(s): Minghui Hu, Chao Zhang, Dajun Zhang, Yanan Sun, Youjin Deng, and Jian-Ping Lv

The phase of spins in the quasi-two-dimensional (q2D) XY model has emerged as a topic of significant interest across multiple subfields of physics. Conventional wisdom, rooted in the Mermin-Wagner theorem and supported by existing paradigms, asserts that true long-range (LR) order is prohibited in q…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237101] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies long-range order in a quasi-2D XY model with short-range interactions, challenging the Mermin-Wagner theorem via critical fluctuations.
motivation: To understand whether true long-range order can exist in quasi-2D systems with only short-range interactions, which is forbidden by the Mermin-Wagner theorem in strictly 2D.
method: Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling analysis of the quasi-2D XY model with weak interlayer coupling.
result: They find evidence of long-range order at finite temperature, attributed to critical fluctuations that stabilize order despite short-range interactions.
conclusion: The quasi-2D XY model can exhibit long-range order, revising conventional understanding of phase transitions in low-dimensional systems.

title: Momentum-Resolved Two-Dimensional Spectroscopy As A Probe Of Nonlinear Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Duilio de Santis, Alex Gómez-Salvador, Nataliia Bazhan, Sebastian Erne, Maximilian Prüfer, Claudio Guarcello, Davide Valenti, Jörg Schmiedmayer, And Eugene Demler
abstract:
Author(s): Duilio De Santis, Alex Gómez-Salvador, Nataliia Bazhan, Sebastian Erne, Maximilian Prüfer, Claudio Guarcello, Davide Valenti, Jörg Schmiedmayer, and Eugene Demler

Emergent collective excitations constitute a hallmark of interacting quantum many-body systems, yet in solid-state platforms their study has been largely limited by the constraints of linear-response probes and by finite momentum resolution. We propose to overcome these limitations by combining the …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233401] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes momentum-resolved two-dimensional spectroscopy to probe nonlinear quantum field dynamics in ultracold atomic gases.
motivation: Linear-response probes and finite momentum resolution limit the study of emergent collective excitations in quantum many-body systems.
method: Combines two-dimensional spectroscopy with momentum resolution, using a sequence of Bragg pulses to excite and probe nonlinear responses.
result: The method enables access to momentum-resolved nonlinear response functions, revealing dynamics beyond linear response.
conclusion: Momentum-resolved 2D spectroscopy is a powerful tool for studying nonlinear quantum field dynamics in ultracold gases.

title: Efimov Effect In Ultracold Microwave-Shielded Polar Molecules
authors: Shayamal Singh And Chris H. Greene
abstract:
Author(s): Shayamal Singh and Chris H. Greene

A quantum-mechanical description is presented for the three-body physics of shielded dipolar molecules, including a prediction of observable Efimov physics. Despite the anisotropic and long-range nature of the interaction, shielding enables a regime in which universality emerges already at the two-b…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233402] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts Efimov physics in ultracold microwave-shielded polar molecules, focusing on three-body bound states.
motivation: To explore universal three-body physics in a novel system of shielded dipolar molecules, where anisotropic long-range interactions are present.
method: Quantum-mechanical three-body calculations using a model potential that accounts for microwave shielding and dipolar interactions.
result: Observation of Efimov resonances and universal scaling behavior despite the anisotropic and long-range nature of the interaction.
conclusion: Microwave-shielded polar molecules provide a new platform for studying Efimov physics and universal three-body phenomena.

title: Proper Theory Of Magnon Orbital Angular Momentum At Equilibrium
abstract:
Author(s): Junyu Tang and Ran Cheng

The orbital motion of chargeless bosons, unlike that of electrons, does not generate a magnetic moment and thus cannot directly interact with magnetic fields. To formulate the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of magnons, we first identify its proper conjugate variable by considering the Aharonov-Cashe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236702] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework for magnon orbital angular momentum at equilibrium by identifying its conjugate variable and deriving a continuity equation.
motivation: Magnons are chargeless bosons whose orbital motion does not generate a magnetic moment, making it challenging to define orbital angular momentum. The authors aim to formulate a proper theory for magnon OAM.
method: The authors identify the conjugate variable of magnon OAM by considering the Aharonov-Casher effect and derive a continuity equation for the OAM density.
result: They obtain a consistent definition of magnon OAM that satisfies conservation laws and can be computed from equilibrium spin textures.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous foundation for magnon OAM, enabling future studies of orbital transport in magnetic insulators.

title: Topological Transition And Emergence Of Elasticity Of Dislocation In Skyrmion Lattice: Beyond Kittel’s Magnetic-Polar Analogy
authors: Kohta Kasai, Akihiro Uematsu, Yu Wang, Tao Xu, Chang Liu, Susumu Minami, And Takahiro Shimada
abstract:
Author(s): Kohta Kasai, Akihiro Uematsu, Yu Wang, Tao Xu, Chang Liu, Susumu Minami, and Takahiro Shimada

Skyrmion dislocations exhibit intrinsic core structures possessing large skyrmion deformation and topological phase transitions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236703] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological transitions and elasticity of dislocations in skyrmion lattices, extending beyond Kittel's magnetic-polar analogy.
motivation: Understanding the core structure and topological phase transitions of skyrmion dislocations is important for spintronic applications.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze dislocation core structures and elastic properties in skyrmion lattices.
result: They find that skyrmion dislocations exhibit intrinsic core structures with large deformation and topological phase transitions.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into the mechanics of skyrmion lattices beyond the traditional analogy.

title: Chiral Spin Liquid Instability Of The Kitaev Honeycomb Model With Crystallographic Defects
authors: Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, And Itamar Kimchi
abstract:
Author(s): Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, and Itamar Kimchi

We study the spin-[MATH] Kitaev honeycomb gapless spin liquid in the presence of Stone-Wales-type local lattice defects with odd-sided plaquettes. While the clean Kitaev model has no finite-temperature phase transitions, we find that introducing a finite defect density [MATH] p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236704] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of Stone-Wales-type lattice defects on the Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid, finding a chiral spin liquid instability at finite defect density.
motivation: To understand how crystallographic defects affect the stability and phase diagram of the Kitaev spin liquid, which is a paradigmatic quantum spin liquid candidate.
method: The authors analyze the Kitaev model with odd-sided plaquettes introduced by Stone-Wales defects using analytical and numerical techniques, likely including mean-field or exact diagonalization.
result: A finite density of defects induces a finite-temperature phase transition to a chiral spin liquid phase, which is absent in the clean model.
conclusion: Defects can qualitatively alter the physics of quantum spin liquids, potentially enabling new topological phases.

title: Boosting Gaussian Boson Sampling Using Optical Parametric Amplification Networks
authors: Yukuan Zhao, Xiao-Ye Xu, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Yukuan Zhao, Xiao-Ye Xu, Chuan-Feng Li, and Guang-Can Guo

Gaussian boson sampling (GBS) provides a route toward demonstrating quantum computational advantage. However, optical loss, which reduces the entanglement in the system, can render GBS results classically simulable. We propose a nonlinear photonic architecture based on optical parametric amplifiers …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062433] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a nonlinear photonic architecture using optical parametric amplifiers to boost Gaussian boson sampling performance under loss.
motivation: Optical loss in Gaussian boson sampling reduces entanglement and can make the output classically simulable, undermining claims of quantum advantage.
method: The authors design a network of optical parametric amplifiers integrated into the GBS setup to counteract loss and enhance non-classical correlations.
result: The proposed architecture improves the robustness of GBS against loss, potentially extending the regime where quantum advantage can be demonstrated.
conclusion: Optical parametric amplification networks offer a practical way to mitigate loss in GBS experiments, but the work is primarily an engineering solution rather than a fundamental advance in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Enhanced Optical Bistability In Conjugate Topological Photonic Crystals
authors: Yu-Peng Li, Yu-Jie Jiang, Xu-Jin Wang, Yong Zhang, Peigang Li, And Jie-Yun Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Peng Li, Yu-Jie Jiang, Xu-Jin Wang, Yong Zhang, Peigang Li, and Jie-Yun Yan

A conjugate topological photonic crystal (CTPC) is designed to achieve highly efficient optical bistability. By exploiting the conjugate topological edge state supported by the CTPC, the structure exhibits a markedly reduced bistability threshold, reaching the level of a few microwatts per meter in …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063519] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates enhanced optical bistability in conjugate topological photonic crystals using topological edge states.
motivation: To achieve low-threshold optical bistability for applications in all-optical switching and signal processing.
method: Designs a conjugate topological photonic crystal (CTPC) that supports a topological edge state, and uses nonlinear optical effects to realize bistability.
result: The CTPC structure exhibits a markedly reduced bistability threshold down to a few microwatts per meter.
conclusion: Conjugate topological photonic crystals provide a promising platform for low-power optical bistability and nonlinear photonic devices.

title: Accelerating Evaporative Cooling Of A Strongly Interacting Fermi Gas By Tilting The Optical Trap With A Magnetic Field Gradient
authors: Bolong Jiao, Shuai Peng, Qinxuan Peng, Shaokun Liu, Mengde Gan, Jiaming Li, And Le Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Bolong Jiao, Shuai Peng, Qinxuan Peng, Shaokun Liu, Mengde Gan, Jiaming Li, and Le Luo

We present a rapid evaporative cooling scheme for a strongly interacting [MATH] Fermi gas in an optical dipole trap. The method uses a magnetic-field-gradient-induced tilt of the trapping potential to accelerate cooling in the unitarity-limited regime. In evaporation based only on lowerin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063314] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to accelerate evaporative cooling of a strongly interacting Fermi gas by tilting the optical trap with a magnetic field gradient.
motivation: Evaporative cooling of ultracold Fermi gases is slow in the unitarity-limited regime; a faster method is needed to improve experimental efficiency.
method: A magnetic field gradient is applied to tilt the optical dipole trap, enhancing the escape of high-energy atoms and thus accelerating the evaporation process.
result: The tilted trap scheme achieves significantly faster cooling rates compared to conventional evaporation, reaching quantum degeneracy in reduced time.
conclusion: The technique provides a practical improvement for producing ultracold Fermi gases, with potential applications in quantum simulation and many-body physics.

title: Optical Echoes Of Light Near An Analog Black Hole
authors: Suting Ju, Jingxuan Zhang, And Li-Gang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Suting Ju, Jingxuan Zhang, and Li-Gang Wang

The light deflection under a strong gravitational field, referred to as strong gravitational lensing, provides a powerful probe of spacetime geometry. Besides, laboratory analog models are employed to study the effects of curved spacetime and explore the design of optical devices. Here, applying the…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063517] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optical echoes near an analog black hole, focusing on gravitational lensing analogies in laboratory systems.
motivation: To explore strong gravitational lensing effects using laboratory analog models and to design optical devices inspired by curved spacetime.
method: The authors apply theoretical modeling of light propagation in an analog black hole setup, analyzing optical echoes and deflection.
result: They demonstrate that analog black holes can produce optical echoes similar to those expected in real gravitational lensing.
conclusion: Analog models provide a useful platform for studying gravitational lensing and may inspire novel optical devices.

title: Diffusion Minimization Via Optimal Smearing In Collapse And Hybrid Classical-quantum Gravitational Models
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolò Piccione

Spontaneous diffusion (i.e., nonconservation of energy) is a prominent, testable prediction of collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models. Without smearing of the mass density operator, the associated heating (or energy increase) rate diverges, yet the smearing distribution is arbitr…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062211] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spontaneous diffusion in collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models, focusing on optimal smearing to minimize heating.
motivation: Spontaneous diffusion leads to energy nonconservation and divergent heating rates in collapse models; smearing the mass density operator can regularize this, but the optimal smearing distribution is unknown.
method: The author derives conditions for minimal heating by analyzing the diffusion rate as a functional of the smearing distribution, using variational techniques.
result: An optimal smearing distribution is found that minimizes the heating rate, and the resulting diffusion is characterized.
conclusion: The work provides a way to make collapse models phenomenologically viable by reducing predicted heating to testable levels.

title: Limitations Of An Approximative Phase-space Description In Strong-field Quantum Optics
authors: Rasmus Vesterager Gothelf, Lars Bojer Madsen, And Christian Saugbjerg Lange
abstract:
Author(s): Rasmus Vesterager Gothelf, Lars Bojer Madsen, and Christian Saugbjerg Lange

In recent years, strong-field processes such as high-order harmonic generation (HHG) and above-threshold ionization driven by nonclassical states of light have become an increasingly popular field of study. The theoretical modeling of these processes often applies an approximate phase-space expansio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063107] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the limitations of an approximate phase-space description in strong-field quantum optics, specifically for high-order harmonic generation and above-threshold ionization driven by nonclassical light.
motivation: Strong-field processes with nonclassical light are gaining interest, but theoretical models often rely on approximate phase-space expansions whose validity is not well understood.
method: The authors analyze the accuracy of the phase-space expansion by comparing it to exact quantum calculations for specific strong-field scenarios.
result: They identify regimes where the approximation breaks down, providing quantitative bounds on its validity.
conclusion: The approximate phase-space description has limited applicability in strong-field quantum optics, and more accurate methods are needed for nonclassical driving fields.

title: Spin Chirality Driven Tunability And Multifunctionality In Two-dimensional Noncollinear Antiferromagnets
authors: Ting Lai, Yongqian Zhu, Jie Zhang, Yuhui Li, Guolin Wan, Xudan Zhang, Jia-Tao Sun, Jinbo Pan, And Shixuan Du
abstract:
Author(s): Ting Lai, Yongqian Zhu, Jie Zhang, Yuhui Li, Guolin Wan, Xudan Zhang, Jia-Tao Sun, Jinbo Pan, and Shixuan Du

Noncollinear antiferromagnets (NCAFs) offer an ideal platform for high-performance spintronic devices. Weak spin-orbit coupling (SOC) magnets, though abundant and important, are overlooked. We propose a symmetry framework for two-dimensional triangular antiferromagnets with [MATH] spin configur…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214434] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin chirality and multifunctionality in two-dimensional noncollinear antiferromagnets, focusing on spintronic applications.
motivation: Noncollinear antiferromagnets are promising for spintronics, but weak spin-orbit coupling magnets have been overlooked; the authors aim to propose a symmetry framework for such materials.
method: The authors develop a symmetry framework for two-dimensional triangular antiferromagnets with noncollinear spin configurations and analyze their electronic and magnetic properties.
result: They demonstrate tunable spin chirality and multifunctionality, including potential for spintronic devices.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for exploiting weak SOC magnets in spintronics, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Topological Phase Transitions By Time-dependent Electromagnetic Fields In Frustrated Magnets: Role Of Dynamical And Static Magnetic Fields
authors: Tatsuya Shirato, Ryota Yambe, And Satoru Hayami
abstract:
Author(s): Tatsuya Shirato, Ryota Yambe, and Satoru Hayami

We theoretically investigate the effects of time-dependent electromagnetic fields on frustrated magnets with the spatial inversion symmetry. Two types of external-field setups are considered. One is a circularly polarized electromagnetic field and the other is a combination of a circularly polarized…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214435] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies topological phase transitions in frustrated magnets driven by time-dependent electromagnetic fields, focusing on dynamical and static magnetic field effects.
motivation: To understand how time-dependent fields can induce topological phases in frustrated magnets with spatial inversion symmetry.
method: Theoretical analysis using two external-field setups: a circularly polarized electromagnetic field and a combination of circularly polarized and static magnetic fields.
result: Identifies conditions for topological phase transitions and characterizes the resulting phases.
conclusion: Time-dependent electromagnetic fields can be used to control topological phases in frustrated magnets, offering a route to manipulate magnetic order.

title: Hall Anomaly In The Mixed State Of type-II Superconductors: Evidence For Vacancies Within Vortex Lattice Domains
authors: Ruonan Guo, Yong-Cong Chen, Da Jiang, And Ping Ao
abstract:
Author(s): Ruonan Guo, Yong-Cong Chen, Da Jiang, and Ping Ao

Despite numerous recent studies on the Hall anomaly following the discovery of cuprate superconductivity, its origin remains contentious. We demonstrate—without invoking adjustable parameters—that a previously proposed mechanism, in which vacancies form within vortex lattice domains, provides a comp…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214513] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a vacancy mechanism within vortex lattice domains to explain the Hall anomaly in type-II superconductors.
motivation: The Hall anomaly in mixed-state type-II superconductors remains contentious; the authors aim to resolve it without adjustable parameters.
method: They demonstrate that vacancies forming within vortex lattice domains can account for the Hall anomaly, using a previously proposed mechanism.
result: The mechanism provides a consistent explanation for the Hall anomaly without invoking adjustable parameters.
conclusion: Vacancies within vortex lattice domains are a plausible origin of the Hall anomaly in type-II superconductors.

title: Revisiting The Symmetry And Optical Phonons Of Altermagnetic $α$-MnTe
authors: Ece Uykur, Marcos V. Gonçalves-Faria, Sahana Rößler, Victoria A. Ginga, Marcus Schmidt, Stephan Winnerl, Manfred Helm, And Alexander A. Tsirlin
abstract:

Using infrared and Raman spectroscopies combined with high-resolution x-ray diffraction, we address several controversial aspects of altermagnetic [MATH]-MnTe. We show that mechanical stress applied to crystals of this material causes a drastic broadening of Bragg peaks that conceals signatures of addi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224107] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the symmetry and optical phonons of altermagnetic α-MnTe using infrared and Raman spectroscopies and high-resolution x-ray diffraction.
motivation: To resolve controversies regarding the crystal symmetry and phonon modes of α-MnTe, which is an altermagnetic material.
method: Combined infrared and Raman spectroscopies with high-resolution x-ray diffraction on single crystals under controlled stress.
result: Mechanical stress broadens Bragg peaks, obscuring additional structural signatures; the phonon spectra are consistent with the P6₃/mmc structure.
conclusion: The study clarifies the symmetry and phonon properties of α-MnTe, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Creation Of Domain-wall Skyrmions In Chiral Magnets With Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert Dynamics And Demagnetization
authors: Sven Bjarke Gudnason, Yuki Amari, And Muneto Nitta
